{{神社| 名称= 春日神社| 画像= | 所在地= 徳島県徳島市眉山町大滝山1| 位置= | 祭神= [[武甕槌命]]、[[斎主命]]、[[天児屋根命]]、[[比売神]]| 社格= | 例祭= [[4月17日]]、[[10月16日]]}}
'''春日神社'''（かすがじんじゃ）は、[[徳島県]][[徳島市]]にある[[神社]]である。[[眉山 (徳島市)|眉山]]山内の大滝山に位置する。
== 祭神 == [[武甕槌命]]、[[斎主命]]、[[天児屋根命]]、[[比売神]]の四柱で、[[奈良県]]の[[春日大社]]と同一の神々祭っている。武甕槌命、斎主命は常陸国鹿島大社に祭られている。
== 歴史 == [[阿波国]][[名東郡]][[入田町|入田]]（現徳島市入田町）に春日祠として存在したが、[[慶長]]年間に[[蜂須賀家政]]が[[徳島藩]]主になり、[[天正]]14年（[[1586年]]）に、[[徳島城]]築城と共に城下の鎮守として、[[名西郡]]入田村（一説には[[名東郡]][[田宮 (徳島市)|田宮村]]）より現在の大滝山東麓（眉山町大滝山1）に奉遷したと伝えられている。
歴代藩主や民からの崇敬により、[[明治]]より[[県社]]に列せられた。
== アクセス == * [[四国旅客鉄道|JR]][[徳島駅]]から車で約5分。
{{DEFAULTSORT:かすかしんしや}} {{shinto-stub}} [[Category:春日神社]] [[Category:徳島県の神社]] [[Category:眉山]]

== 歴史 == [[阿波国]][[名東郡]][[入田町|入田]]（現徳島市入田町）に春日祠として存在したが、[[慶長]]年間に[[蜂須賀家政]]が[[徳島藩]]主になり、[[天正]]14年（[[1586年]]）に、[[徳島城]]築城と共に城下の鎮守として、[[名西郡]]入田村（一説には[[名東郡]][[田宮 (徳島市)|田宮村]]）より現在の大滝山東麓（眉山町大滝山1）に奉遷したと伝えられている。
歴代藩主や民からの崇敬により、[[明治]]より[[県社]]に列せられた。

{{神社 |名称= 春日神社 |画像= [[ファイル:Kasuga Shinto shrine(Tokushima City).jpg|250px]] |所在地= [[徳島県]][[徳島市]]眉山町大滝山1 |位置={{ウィキ座標2段度分秒|34|04|19.9|N|134|32|33.4|E|scale:25000}} |祭神= [[武甕槌命]]、[[斎主命]]、[[天児屋根命]]、[[比売神]] |社格= 旧県社 |創建= |本殿=[[春日造]] |例祭= [[4月17日]]、[[10月16日]] |神事= }}
'''春日神社'''（かすがじんじゃ）は、[[徳島県]][[徳島市]]にある[[神社]]である。[[眉山 (徳島市)|眉山]]東麓の大滝山に位置する。
== 祭神 == [[武甕槌命]]、[[斎主命]]、[[天児屋根命]]、[[比売神]]の4[[柱]]で、[[奈良県]]の[[春日大社]]と同じ神々を祀っている。
== 歴史 == [[大和国]]春日社領の[[富田庄]]（[[阿波国]][[名東郡]]入田村（現徳島市[[入田町]]）一帯）に[[勧請]]された春日祠に起源を有つといい、[[蜂須賀家政]]の阿波入部に際して現在の大滝山東麓（眉山町大滝山1）に[[遷座]]されたと伝えるが（[[文化 (日本)|文化]]12年（1815年）の『[[阿波志]]』）、一説に[[天正]]14年（[[1586年]]）の家政による[[徳島城]]築城と共に、城下の[[鎮守]]として[[名東郡]][[田宮 (徳島市)|田宮村]]から迎えられ、同村から共に遷された勝福寺（通称春日寺）<ref>当神社境内にあったが、明治初年に廃されたという。</ref>を[[別当寺]]とするようになったともいう（[[昭和]]48年（1973年）の『徳島市史』）。[[慶長|慶長年間]]（16世紀末から17世紀初）に蜂須賀氏が[[徳島藩|徳島藩主]]となって以後、「春日大明神」と称して歴代藩主からの崇敬を受け、祭祀料として毎年供米10石が春日寺充てに寄進されたという。
[[明治]]6年（[[1873年]]）に現社名に改め、[[県社]]に列せられた。境内には[[眉山湧水群]]のひとつ春日水がある。周辺には[[三島神社 (徳島市)|三島神社]]、[[諏訪神社 (徳島市)|諏訪神社]]がある。
== 末社 == 3社
== 市中五社 == * [[諏訪神社 (徳島市)|諏訪神社]] - 徳島市南佐古町 * [[四所神社 (徳島市)|四所神社]] - 徳島市福島町 * [[八幡神社 (徳島市)|八幡神社]] - 徳島市伊賀町 * [[金刀比羅神社 (徳島市)|金刀比羅神社]] - 徳島市勢見町
== 交通 == * [[四国旅客鉄道|JR]][[徳島駅]]から車で約5分。
== 脚注 == {{reflist}}
== 関連項目 == * [[春日神社]] * [[眉山 (徳島市)]]
== 外部リンク == * [http://kamnavi.jp/en/awa/kasuga.htm 春日神社]（個人サイト（神奈備））
{{shinto-stub}} {{DEFAULTSORT:かすかしんしや}} [[Category:徳島市の神社]] [[Category:府県社]] [[Category:春日神社]] [[Category:眉山]]

== 祭神 == [[武甕槌命]]、[[斎主命]]、[[天児屋根命]]、[[比売神]]の4[[柱]]で、[[奈良県]]の[[春日大社]]と同じ神々を祀っている。
== 歴史 == [[大和国]]春日社領の[[富田庄]]（[[阿波国]][[名東郡]]入田村（現徳島市[[入田町]]）一帯）に[[勧請]]された春日祠に起源を有つといい、[[蜂須賀家政]]の阿波入部に際して現在の大滝山東麓（眉山町大滝山1）に[[遷座]]されたと伝えるが（[[文化 (元号)|文化]]12年（1815年）の『[[阿波志]]』）、一説に[[天正]]14年（[[1586年]]）の家政による[[徳島城]]築城と共に、城下の[[鎮守]]として[[名東郡]]田宮村から迎えられ、同村から共に遷された勝福寺（通称春日寺）<ref>当神社境内にあったが、明治初年に廃されたという。</ref>を[[別当寺]]とするようになったともいう（[[昭和]]48年（1973年）の『徳島市史』）。[[慶長|慶長年間]]（16世紀末から17世紀初）に蜂須賀氏が[[徳島藩|徳島藩主]]となって以後、「春日大明神」と称して歴代藩主からの崇敬を受け、祭祀料として毎年供米10石が春日寺充てに寄進されたという。
[[明治]]6年（[[1873年]]）に現社名に改め、[[県社]]に列せられた。境内には[[眉山湧水群]]のひとつ春日水がある。周辺には[[三島神社 (徳島市)|三島神社]]、[[諏訪神社 (徳島市)|諏訪神社]]がある。
== 境内社 == * 豊玉比賣神社（祭神・天石門別豊玉比賣（[[トヨタマヒメ]]）、式内社） ** [[徳島城]]内にあった竜王神社が[[国瑞彦神社]]に合祀された後、さらに当神社に移され、合祀となった。 * 若宮神社（祭神・[[天忍雲根命]]） * 秋葉神社（祭神・[[天照大御神]]、[[大巳貴命]]、[[波邇夜須毘売神|埴安姫神]]、[[保食神]]、[[少彦名命]]）
== 交通 == * [[四国旅客鉄道|JR]][[徳島駅]]から車で約5分。
== 脚注 == {{脚注ヘルプ}} {{reflist}}
== 関連項目 == * 徳島市中五社 ** [[諏訪神社 (徳島市)|諏訪神社]] - 徳島市[[南佐古三番町]] ** [[四所神社 (徳島市)|四所神社]] - 徳島市[[福島 (徳島市)|福島]] ** [[八幡神社 (徳島市)|八幡神社]] - 徳島市[[伊賀町 (徳島市)|伊賀町]] ** [[金刀比羅神社 (徳島市)|金刀比羅神社]] - 徳島市[[勢見町]] {{shinto-stub}} {{神道 横}} {{DEFAULTSORT:かすかしんしや とくしまし}} [[Category:徳島県の旧県社]] [[Category:徳島市の神社]] [[Category:春日神社]] [[Category:眉山]]

{{otheruses|Shinto shrines in Myozan, Tokushima City, Tokushima Prefecture|a shrine in Shimosuketo, Tokushima City|Kasuga Shrine (Shimosuketo, Tokushima)}} {{Infobox Shinto shrine | name = Kasuga Shrine (春日神社) | religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]] |image = [[File:Kasuga Jinjya.jpeg|250px]] | location = {{ill|Myozan, Tokushima City|ja|眉山町}}, {{ill|Tokushima Prefecture|ja|徳島県}}, Japan | coordinates = {{Coord|34|04|19.9|N|134|32|33.4|E|scale:25000|display=inline,title}} | deity = {{ill|Takemikazuchi|ja|武甕槌命}}, {{ill|Izanagi-no-Mikoto|ja|斎主命}}, {{ill|Amenokoyane no Mikoto|ja|天児屋根命}}, {{ill|Hime no Kami|ja|比売神}} | rank = Former {{ill|Ken-sha|ja|県社}} | founded = 1586 (Tenshō 14) | main_building = {{ill|Kasuga-zukuri|ja|春日造}} | festivals = {{ill|April 17|ja|4月17日}}, {{ill|October 17|ja|10月17日}} }}
[[File:Kasugasui.jpeg|thumb|250px|right|Kasuga Spring (春日水)]] '''Kasuga Shrine''' (春日神社) is a {{ill|Shinto shrine|ja|神社}} located in {{ill|Myozan, Tokushima City|ja|眉山町}}, {{ill|Tokushima Prefecture|ja|徳島県}}, Japan. It is situated on the eastern foothills of {{ill|Mount Bizan|ja|眉山}}.
== Deities == The shrine enshrines the following four {{ill|Kami|ja|柱}} (deities), identical to those of {{ill|Kasuga Taisha|ja|春日大社|Kasuga-taisha}} in {{ill|Nara Prefecture|ja|奈良県}}: * {{ill|Takemikazuchi|ja|武甕槌命}} * {{ill|Izanagi-no-Mikoto|ja|斎主命}} * {{ill|Amenokoyane no Mikoto|ja|天児屋根命}} * {{ill|Hime no Kami|ja|比売神}}
== History == The shrine traces its origins to a {{ill|Kasuga Shrine|ja|春日祠}} enshrined at the Kasuga territory in {{ill|Tomi-da|ja|富田庄}} (modern {{ill|Irida|ja|入田町}}, Tokushima City), a former estate of Kasuga Shrine in {{ill|Yamato Province|ja|大和国}}. It is said to have been relocated to its current site at Otakiyama during the transfer of power to the {{ill|Hachisuka clan|ja|蜂須賀氏}} in 1586, coinciding with the construction of {{ill|Tokushima Castle|ja|徳島城}}. Another account suggests the shrine was moved from {{ill|Tamiya Village|ja|田宮村}} along with Shofuku-ji Temple, which later became the shrine’s {{ill|Bettōji|ja|別当寺}} before its abolition in the early {{ill|Meiji period|ja|明治時代}}.<ref>According to the ''Awa-shi'' (阿波志), compiled in 1815.</ref>
During the {{ill|Keicho era|ja|慶長}} (late 16th to early 17th century), the shrine was referred to as "Kasuga Daimyōjin" and received significant patronage from the Hachisuka clan, including an annual offering of 10 koku of rice. In 1873, it was officially renamed Kasuga Shrine and designated as a {{ill|Ken-sha|ja|県社}}. The shrine also features "Kasuga Spring" (春日水), one of the notable {{ill|Mount Bizan springs|ja|眉山湧水群}}.
== Sub-Shrines == The shrine complex includes the following sub-shrines: * '''Toyotama-hime Shrine''' (deity: {{ill|Toyotama-hime|ja|豊玉比賣}}) * Enshrines the deity formerly worshipped at Ryuo Shrine within Tokushima Castle. * '''Wakamiya Shrine''' (deity: {{ill|Ame-no-Kumunushi|ja|天忍雲根命}}) * '''Akiba Shrine''' (deity: {{ill|Amaterasu|ja|天照大御神}}, {{ill|Onamuchi|ja|大巳貴命}}, {{ill|Haniyasubime|ja|埴安姫神}}, {{ill|Ukemochi|ja|保食神}}, {{ill|Sukunabikona|ja|少彦名命}})
== Transportation == * '''By car''': 5 minutes from {{ill|Tokushima Station|ja|徳島駅}}, {{ill|Shikoku Railway Company|ja|四国旅客鉄道}} (JR Shikoku).
== References == {{reflist}}
== Related Shrines == * '''Tokushima City Nakago-sha''' (中五社) * {{ill|Suwa Shrine (Tokushima)|ja|諏訪神社 (徳島市)}} - Minami-Sako 3-chome * {{ill|Shisho Shrine (Tokushima)|ja|四所神社 (徳島市)}} - Fukushima, Tokushima * {{ill|Hachiman Shrine (Tokushima)|ja|八幡神社 (徳島市)}} - Iga-cho, Tokushima * {{ill|Kotohira Shrine (Tokushima)|ja|金刀比羅神社 (徳島市)}} - Semimachi, Tokushima

[[File:Kasugasui.jpeg|thumb|250px|right|Kasuga Spring (春日水)]] '''Kasuga Shrine''' (春日神社) is a {{ill|Shinto shrine|ja|神社}} located in {{ill|Myozan, Tokushima City|ja|眉山町}}, {{ill|Tokushima Prefecture|ja|徳島県}}, Japan. It is situated on the eastern foothills of {{ill|Mount Bizan|ja|眉山}}.
== Deities == The shrine enshrines the following four {{ill|Kami|ja|柱}} (deities), identical to those of {{ill|Kasuga Taisha|ja|春日大社|Kasuga-taisha}} in {{ill|Nara Prefecture|ja|奈良県}}: * {{ill|Takemikazuchi|ja|武甕槌命}} * {{ill|Izanagi-no-Mikoto|ja|斎主命}} * {{ill|Amenokoyane no Mikoto|ja|天児屋根命}} * {{ill|Hime no Kami|ja|比売神}}
== History == The shrine traces its origins to a {{ill|Kasuga Shrine|ja|春日祠}} enshrined at the Kasuga territory in {{ill|Tomi-da|ja|富田庄}} (modern {{ill|Irida|ja|入田町}}, Tokushima City), a former estate of Kasuga Shrine in {{ill|Yamato Province|ja|大和国}}. It is said to have been relocated to its current site at Otakiyama during the transfer of power to the {{ill|Hachisuka clan|ja|蜂須賀氏}} in 1586, coinciding with the construction of {{ill|Tokushima Castle|ja|徳島城}}. Another account suggests the shrine was moved from {{ill|Tamiya Village|ja|田宮村}} along with Shofuku-ji Temple, which later became the shrine’s {{ill|Bettōji|ja|別当寺}} before its abolition in the early {{ill|Meiji period|ja|明治時代}}.<ref>According to the ''Awa-shi'' (阿波志), compiled in 1815.</ref>
During the {{ill|Keicho era|ja|慶長}} (late 16th to early 17th century), the shrine was referred to as "Kasuga Daimyōjin" and received significant patronage from the Hachisuka clan, including an annual offering of 10 koku of rice. In 1873, it was officially renamed Kasuga Shrine and designated as a {{ill|Ken-sha|ja|県社}}. The shrine also features "Kasuga Spring" (春日水), one of the notable {{ill|Mount Bizan springs|ja|眉山湧水群}}.
== Sub-Shrines == The shrine complex includes the following sub-shrines: * '''Toyotama-hime Shrine''' (deity: {{ill|Toyotama-hime|ja|豊玉比賣}}) * Enshrines the deity formerly worshipped at Ryuo Shrine within Tokushima Castle. * '''Wakamiya Shrine''' (deity: {{ill|Ame-no-Kumunushi|ja|天忍雲根命}}) * '''Akiba Shrine''' (deity: {{ill|Amaterasu|ja|天照大御神}}, {{ill|Onamuchi|ja|大巳貴命}}, {{ill|Haniyasubime|ja|埴安姫神}}, {{ill|Ukemochi|ja|保食神}}, {{ill|Sukunabikona|ja|少彦名命}})
== Transportation == * '''By car''': 5 minutes from {{ill|Tokushima Station|ja|徳島駅}}, {{ill|Shikoku Railway Company|ja|四国旅客鉄道}} (JR Shikoku).
== References == {{reflist}}
== Related Shrines == * '''Tokushima City Nakago-sha''' (中五社) * {{ill|Suwa Shrine (Tokushima)|ja|諏訪神社 (徳島市)}} - Minami-Sako 3-chome * {{ill|Shisho Shrine (Tokushima)|ja|四所神社 (徳島市)}} - Fukushima, Tokushima * {{ill|Hachiman Shrine (Tokushima)|ja|八幡神社 (徳島市)}} - Iga-cho, Tokushima * {{ill|Kotohira Shrine (Tokushima)|ja|金刀比羅神社 (徳島市)}} - Semimachi, Tokushima

[[File:Kasugasui.jpeg|thumb|250px|right|Kasuga Spring (春日水)]] '''Kasuga Shrine''' (春日神社) is a {{ill|Shinto shrine|ja|神社}} located in {{ill|Myozan, Tokushima City|ja|眉山町}}, {{ill|Tokushima Prefecture|ja|徳島県}}, Japan. It is situated on the eastern foothills of {{ill|Mount Bizan|ja|眉山}}.
== Deities == The shrine enshrines the following four {{ill|Kami|ja|柱}} (deities), identical to those of {{ill|Kasuga Taisha|ja|春日大社|Kasuga-taisha}} in {{ill|Nara Prefecture|ja|奈良県}}: * {{ill|Takemikazuchi|ja|武甕槌命}} * {{ill|Izanagi-no-Mikoto|ja|斎主命}} * {{ill|Amenokoyane no Mikoto|ja|天児屋根命}} * {{ill|Hime no Kami|ja|比売神}}
== History == The shrine traces its origins to a {{ill|Kasuga Shrine|ja|春日祠}} enshrined at the Kasuga territory in {{ill|Tomi-da|ja|富田庄}} (modern {{ill|Irida|ja|入田町}}, Tokushima City), a former estate of Kasuga Shrine in {{ill|Yamato Province|ja|大和国}}. It is said to have been relocated to its current site at Otakiyama during the transfer of power to the {{ill|Hachisuka clan|ja|蜂須賀氏}} in 1586, coinciding with the construction of {{ill|Tokushima Castle|ja|徳島城}}. Another account suggests the shrine was moved from {{ill|Tamiya Village|ja|田宮村}} along with Shofuku-ji Temple, which later became the shrine’s {{ill|Bettōji|ja|別当寺}} before its abolition in the early {{ill|Meiji period|ja|明治時代}}.<ref>According to the ''Awa-shi'' (阿波志), compiled in 1815.</ref>
During the {{ill|Keicho era|ja|慶長}} (late 16th to early 17th century), the shrine was referred to as "Kasuga Daimyōjin" and received significant patronage from the Hachisuka clan, including an annual offering of 10 koku of rice. In 1873, it was officially renamed Kasuga Shrine and designated as a {{ill|Ken-sha|ja|県社}}. The shrine also features "Kasuga Spring" (春日水), one of the notable {{ill|Mount Bizan springs|ja|眉山湧水群}}.
== Sub-Shrines == The shrine complex includes the following sub-shrines: * '''Toyotama-hime Shrine''' (deity: {{ill|Toyotama-hime|ja|豊玉比賣}}) * Enshrines the deity formerly worshipped at Ryuo Shrine within Tokushima Castle. * '''Wakamiya Shrine''' (deity: {{ill|Ame-no-Kumunushi|ja|天忍雲根命}}) * '''Akiba Shrine''' (deity: {{ill|Amaterasu|ja|天照大御神}}, {{ill|Onamuchi|ja|大巳貴命}}, {{ill|Haniyasubime|ja|埴安姫神}}, {{ill|Ukemochi|ja|保食神}}, {{ill|Sukunabikona|ja|少彦名命}})
== Transportation == * '''By car''': 5 minutes from {{ill|Tokushima Station|ja|徳島駅}}, {{ill|Shikoku Railway Company|ja|四国旅客鉄道}} (JR Shikoku).
== References == {{reflist}}
== Related Shrines == * '''Tokushima City Nakago-sha''' (中五社) * {{ill|Suwa Shrine (Tokushima)|ja|諏訪神社 (徳島市)}} - Minami-Sako 3-chome * {{ill|Shisho Shrine (Tokushima)|ja|四所神社 (徳島市)}} - Fukushima, Tokushima * {{ill|Hachiman Shrine (Tokushima)|ja|八幡神社 (徳島市)}} - Iga-cho, Tokushima * {{ill|Kotohira Shrine (Tokushima)|ja|金刀比羅神社 (徳島市)}} - Semimachi, Tokushima

[[File:Kasugasui.jpeg|thumb|250px|right|Kasuga Spring (春日水)]] '''Kasuga Shrine''' (春日神社) is a {{ill|Shinto shrine|ja|神社}} located in {{ill|Myozan, Tokushima City|ja|眉山町}}, {{ill|Tokushima Prefecture|ja|徳島県}}, Japan. It is situated on the eastern foothills of {{ill|Mount Bizan|ja|眉山}}.
== Deities == The shrine enshrines the following four {{ill|Kami|ja|柱}} (deities), identical to those of {{ill|Kasuga Taisha|ja|春日大社|Kasuga-taisha}} in {{ill|Nara Prefecture|ja|奈良県}}: * {{ill|Takemikazuchi|ja|武甕槌命}} * {{ill|Izanagi-no-Mikoto|ja|斎主命}} * {{ill|Amenokoyane no Mikoto|ja|天児屋根命}} * {{ill|Hime no Kami|ja|比売神}}
== History == The shrine traces its origins to a {{ill|Kasuga Shrine|ja|春日祠}} enshrined at the Kasuga territory in {{ill|Tomi-da|ja|富田庄}} (modern {{ill|Irida|ja|入田町}}, Tokushima City), a former estate of Kasuga Shrine in {{ill|Yamato Province|ja|大和国}}. It is said to have been relocated to its current site at Otakiyama during the transfer of power to the {{ill|Hachisuka clan|ja|蜂須賀氏}} in 1586, coinciding with the construction of {{ill|Tokushima Castle|ja|徳島城}}. Another account suggests the shrine was moved from {{ill|Tamiya Village|ja|田宮村}} along with Shofuku-ji Temple, which later became the shrine’s {{ill|Bettōji|ja|別当寺}} before its abolition in the early {{ill|Meiji period|ja|明治時代}}.<ref>According to the ''Awa-shi'' (阿波志), compiled in 1815.</ref>
During the {{ill|Keicho era|ja|慶長}} (late 16th to early 17th century), the shrine was referred to as "Kasuga Daimyōjin" and received significant patronage from the Hachisuka clan, including an annual offering of 10 koku of rice. In 1873, it was officially renamed Kasuga Shrine and designated as a {{ill|Ken-sha|ja|県社}}. The shrine also features "Kasuga Spring" (春日水), one of the notable {{ill|Mount Bizan springs|ja|眉山湧水群}}.
== Sub-Shrines == The shrine complex includes the following sub-shrines: * '''Toyotama-hime Shrine''' (deity: {{ill|Toyotama-hime|ja|豊玉比賣}}) * Enshrines the deity formerly worshipped at Ryuo Shrine within Tokushima Castle. * '''Wakamiya Shrine''' (deity: {{ill|Ame-no-Kumunushi|ja|天忍雲根命}}) * '''Akiba Shrine''' (deity: {{ill|Amaterasu|ja|天照大御神}}, {{ill|Onamuchi|ja|大巳貴命}}, {{ill|Haniyasubime|ja|埴安姫神}}, {{ill|Ukemochi|ja|保食神}}, {{ill|Sukunabikona|ja|少彦名命}})
== Transportation == * '''By car''': 5 minutes from {{ill|Tokushima Station|ja|徳島駅}}, {{ill|Shikoku Railway Company|ja|四国旅客鉄道}} (JR Shikoku).
== References == {{reflist}}
== Related Shrines == * '''Tokushima City Nakago-sha''' (中五社) * {{ill|Suwa Shrine (Tokushima)|ja|諏訪神社 (徳島市)}} - Minami-Sako 3-chome * {{ill|Shisho Shrine (Tokushima)|ja|四所神社 (徳島市)}} - Fukushima, Tokushima * {{ill|Hachiman Shrine (Tokushima)|ja|八幡神社 (徳島市)}} - Iga-cho, Tokushima * {{ill|Kotohira Shrine (Tokushima)|ja|金刀比羅神社 (徳島市)}} - Semimachi, Tokushima

In 1873, it was officially renamed Kasuga Shrine and designated as a {{ill|Ken-sha|ja|県社}}. The shrine also features "Kasuga Spring" (春日水), one of the notable {{ill|Mount Bizan springs|ja|眉山湧水群}}.

{{otheruses|Shinto shrines in Myozan, Tokushima City, Tokushima Prefecture|a shrine in Shimosuketo, Tokushima City|Kasuga Shrine (Shimosuketo, Tokushima)}} {{Infobox Shinto shrine | name = Kasuga Shrine (春日神社) | religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]] |image = [[File:Kasuga Jinjya.jpeg|250px]] | location = {{ill|Myozan, Tokushima City|ja|眉山町}}, {{ill|Tokushima Prefecture|ja|徳島県}}, Japan | coordinates = {{Coord|34|04|19.9|N|134|32|33.4|E|scale:25000|display=inline,title}} | deity = {{ill|Takemikazuchi|ja|武甕槌命}}, {{ill|Izanagi-no-Mikoto|ja|斎主命}}, {{ill|Amenokoyane no Mikoto|ja|天児屋根命}}, {{ill|Hime no Kami|ja|比売神}} | rank = Former {{ill|Ken-sha|ja|県社}} | founded = 1586 (Tenshō 14) | main_building = {{ill|Kasuga-zukuri|ja|春日造}} | festivals = {{ill|April 17|ja|4月17日}}, {{ill|October 17|ja|10月17日}} }}
[[File:Kasugasui.jpeg|thumb|250px|right|Kasuga Spring (春日水)]] '''Kasuga Shrine''' (春日神社) is a {{ill|Shinto shrine|ja|神社}} located in {{ill|Myozan, Tokushima City|ja|眉山町}}, {{ill|Tokushima Prefecture|ja|徳島県}}, Japan. It is situated on the eastern foothills of {{ill|Mount Bizan|ja|眉山}}.
== Deities == The shrine enshrines the following four {{ill|Kami|ja|柱}} (deities), identical to those of {{ill|Kasuga Taisha|ja|春日大社|Kasuga-taisha}} in {{ill|Nara Prefecture|ja|奈良県}}: * {{ill|Takemikazuchi|ja|武甕槌命}} * {{ill|Izanagi-no-Mikoto|ja|斎主命}} * {{ill|Amenokoyane no Mikoto|ja|天児屋根命}} * {{ill|Hime no Kami|ja|比売神}}
== History == The shrine traces its origins to a {{ill|Kasuga Shrine|ja|春日祠}} enshrined at the Kasuga territory in {{ill|Tomi-da|ja|富田庄}} (modern {{ill|Irida|ja|入田町}}, Tokushima City), a former estate of Kasuga Shrine in {{ill|Yamato Province|ja|大和国}}. It is said to have been relocated to its current site at Otakiyama during the transfer of power to the {{ill|Hachisuka clan|ja|蜂須賀氏}} in 1586, coinciding with the construction of {{ill|Tokushima Castle|ja|徳島城}}. Another account suggests the shrine was moved from {{ill|Tamiya Village|ja|田宮村}} along with Shofuku-ji Temple, which later became the shrine’s {{ill|Bettōji|ja|別当寺}} before its abolition in the early {{ill|Meiji period|ja|明治時代}}.<ref>According to the ''Awa-shi'' (阿波志), compiled in 1815.</ref>
During the {{ill|Keicho era|ja|慶長}} (late 16th to early 17th century), the shrine was referred to as "Kasuga Daimyōjin" and received significant patronage from the Hachisuka clan, including an annual offering of 10 koku of rice. In 1873, it was officially renamed Kasuga Shrine and designated as a {{ill|Ken-sha|ja|県社}}. The shrine also features "Kasuga Spring" (春日水), one of the notable {{ill|Mount Bizan springs|ja|眉山湧水群}}.
== Sub-Shrines == The shrine complex includes the following sub-shrines: * '''Toyotama-hime Shrine''' (deity: {{ill|Toyotama-hime|ja|豊玉比賣}}) * Enshrines the deity formerly worshipped at Ryuo Shrine within Tokushima Castle. * '''Wakamiya Shrine''' (deity: {{ill|Ame-no-Kumunushi|ja|天忍雲根命}}) * '''Akiba Shrine''' (deity: {{ill|Amaterasu|ja|天照大御神}}, {{ill|Onamuchi|ja|大巳貴命}}, {{ill|Haniyasubime|ja|埴安姫神}}, {{ill|Ukemochi|ja|保食神}}, {{ill|Sukunabikona|ja|少彦名命}})
== Transportation == * '''By car''': 5 minutes from {{ill|Tokushima Station|ja|徳島駅}}, {{ill|Shikoku Railway Company|ja|四国旅客鉄道}} (JR Shikoku).
== References == {{reflist}}
== Related Shrines == * '''Tokushima City Nakago-sha''' (中五社) * {{ill|Suwa Shrine (Tokushima)|ja|諏訪神社 (徳島市)}} - Minami-Sako 3-chome * {{ill|Shisho Shrine (Tokushima)|ja|四所神社 (徳島市)}} - Fukushima, Tokushima * {{ill|Hachiman Shrine (Tokushima)|ja|八幡神社 (徳島市)}} - Iga-cho, Tokushima * {{ill|Kotohira Shrine (Tokushima)|ja|金刀比羅神社 (徳島市)}} - Semimachi, Tokushima

{{otheruses|Shinto shrines in Myozan, Tokushima City, Tokushima Prefecture|a shrine in Shimosuketo, Tokushima City|Kasuga Shrine (Shimosuketo, Tokushima)}} {{Infobox Shinto shrine | name = Kasuga Shrine (春日神社) | religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]] |image = [[File:Kasuga Jinjya.jpeg|250px]] | location = {{ill|Myozan, Tokushima City|ja|眉山町}}, {{ill|Tokushima Prefecture|ja|徳島県}}, Japan | coordinates = {{Coord|34|04|19.9|N|134|32|33.4|E|scale:25000|display=inline,title}} | deity = {{ill|Takemikazuchi|ja|武甕槌命}}, {{ill|Izanagi-no-Mikoto|ja|斎主命}}, {{ill|Amenokoyane no Mikoto|ja|天児屋根命}}, {{ill|Hime no Kami|ja|比売神}} | rank = Former {{ill|Ken-sha|ja|県社}} | founded = 1586 (Tenshō 14) | main_building = {{ill|Kasuga-zukuri|ja|春日造}} | festivals = {{ill|April 17|ja|4月17日}}, {{ill|October 17|ja|10月17日}} }}
[[File:Kasugasui.jpeg|thumb|250px|right|Kasuga Spring (春日水)]] '''Kasuga Shrine''' (春日神社) is a {{ill|Shinto shrine|ja|神社}} located in {{ill|Myozan, Tokushima City|ja|眉山町}}, {{ill|Tokushima Prefecture|ja|徳島県}}, Japan. It is situated on the eastern foothills of {{ill|Mount Bizan|ja|眉山}}.
== Deities == The shrine enshrines the following four {{ill|Kami|ja|柱}} (deities), identical to those of {{ill|Kasuga Taisha|ja|春日大社|Kasuga-taisha}} in {{ill|Nara Prefecture|ja|奈良県}}: * {{ill|Takemikazuchi|ja|武甕槌命}} * {{ill|Izanagi-no-Mikoto|ja|斎主命}} * {{ill|Amenokoyane no Mikoto|ja|天児屋根命}} * {{ill|Hime no Kami|ja|比売神}}
== History == The shrine traces its origins to a {{ill|Kasuga Shrine|ja|春日祠}} enshrined at the Kasuga territory in {{ill|Tomi-da|ja|富田庄}} (modern {{ill|Irida|ja|入田町}}, Tokushima City), a former estate of Kasuga Shrine in {{ill|Yamato Province|ja|大和国}}. It is said to have been relocated to its current site at Otakiyama during the transfer of power to the {{ill|Hachisuka clan|ja|蜂須賀氏}} in 1586, coinciding with the construction of {{ill|Tokushima Castle|ja|徳島城}}. Another account suggests the shrine was moved from {{ill|Tamiya Village|ja|田宮村}} along with Shofuku-ji Temple, which later became the shrine’s {{ill|Bettōji|ja|別当寺}} before its abolition in the early {{ill|Meiji period|ja|明治時代}}.<ref>According to the ''Awa-shi'' (阿波志), compiled in 1815.</ref>
During the {{ill|Keicho era|ja|慶長}} (late 16th to early 17th century), the shrine was referred to as "Kasuga Daimyōjin" and received significant patronage from the Hachisuka clan, including an annual offering of 10 koku of rice. In 1873, it was officially renamed Kasuga Shrine and designated as a {{ill|Ken-sha|ja|県社}}. The shrine also features "Kasuga Spring" (春日水), one of the notable {{ill|Mount Bizan springs|ja|眉山湧水群}}.
== Sub-Shrines == The shrine complex includes the following sub-shrines: * '''Toyotama-hime Shrine''' (deity: {{ill|Toyotama-hime|ja|豊玉比賣}}) * Enshrines the deity formerly worshipped at Ryuo Shrine within Tokushima Castle. * '''Wakamiya Shrine''' (deity: {{ill|Ame-no-Kumunushi|ja|天忍雲根命}}) * '''Akiba Shrine''' (deity: {{ill|Amaterasu|ja|天照大御神}}, {{ill|Onamuchi|ja|大巳貴命}}, {{ill|Haniyasubime|ja|埴安姫神}}, {{ill|Ukemochi|ja|保食神}}, {{ill|Sukunabikona|ja|少彦名命}})
== Transportation == * '''By car''': 5 minutes from {{ill|Tokushima Station|ja|徳島駅}}, {{ill|Shikoku Railway Company|ja|四国旅客鉄道}} (JR Shikoku).
== References == {{reflist}}
== Related Shrines == * '''Tokushima City Nakago-sha''' (中五社) * {{ill|Suwa Shrine (Tokushima)|ja|諏訪神社 (徳島市)}} - Minami-Sako 3-chome * {{ill|Shisho Shrine (Tokushima)|ja|四所神社 (徳島市)}} - Fukushima, Tokushima * {{ill|Hachiman Shrine (Tokushima)|ja|八幡神社 (徳島市)}} - Iga-cho, Tokushima * {{ill|Kotohira Shrine (Tokushima)|ja|金刀比羅神社 (徳島市)}} - Semimachi, Tokushima

== Deities == The shrine enshrines the following four {{ill|Kami|ja|柱}} (deities), identical to those of {{ill|Kasuga Taisha|ja|春日大社|1=Kasuga-taisha}} in {{ill|Nara Prefecture|ja|奈良県}}: * {{ill|Takemikazuchi|ja|武甕槌命}} * {{ill|Izanagi-no-Mikoto|ja|斎主命}} * {{ill|Amenokoyane no Mikoto|ja|天児屋根命}} * {{ill|Hime no Kami|ja|比売神}}
== History == The shrine traces its origins to a {{ill|Kasuga Shrine|ja|春日祠}} enshrined at the Kasuga territory in {{ill|Tomi-da|ja|富田庄}} (modern {{ill|Irida|ja|入田町}}, Tokushima City), a former estate of Kasuga Shrine in {{ill|Yamato Province|ja|大和国}}. It is said to have been relocated to its current site at Otakiyama during the transfer of power to the {{ill|Hachisuka clan|ja|蜂須賀氏}} in 1586, coinciding with the construction of {{ill|Tokushima Castle|ja|徳島城}}. Another account suggests the shrine was moved from {{ill|Tamiya Village|ja|田宮村}} along with Shofuku-ji Temple, which later became the shrine’s {{ill|Bettōji|ja|別当寺}} before its abolition in the early {{ill|Meiji period|ja|明治時代}}.<ref>According to the ''Awa-shi'' (阿波志), compiled in 1815.</ref>
During the {{ill|Keicho era|ja|慶長}} (late 16th to early 17th century), the shrine was referred to as "Kasuga Daimyōjin" and received significant patronage from the Hachisuka clan, including an annual offering of 10 koku of rice. In 1873, it was officially renamed Kasuga Shrine and designated as a {{ill|Ken-sha|ja|県社}}. The shrine also features "Kasuga Spring" (春日水), one of the notable {{ill|Mount Bizan springs|ja|眉山湧水群}}.
== Sub-Shrines == The shrine complex includes the following sub-shrines: * '''Toyotama-hime Shrine''' (deity: {{ill|Toyotama-hime|ja|豊玉比賣}}) * Enshrines the deity formerly worshipped at Ryuo Shrine within Tokushima Castle. * '''Wakamiya Shrine''' (deity: {{ill|Ame-no-Kumunushi|ja|天忍雲根命}}) * '''Akiba Shrine''' (deity: {{ill|Amaterasu|ja|天照大御神}}, {{ill|Onamuchi|ja|大巳貴命}}, {{ill|Haniyasubime|ja|埴安姫神}}, {{ill|Ukemochi|ja|保食神}}, {{ill|Sukunabikona|ja|少彦名命}})
== Transportation == * '''By car''': 5 minutes from {{ill|Tokushima Station|ja|徳島駅}}, {{ill|Shikoku Railway Company|ja|四国旅客鉄道}} (JR Shikoku).
== References == {{reflist}}
== Related Shrines == * '''Tokushima City Nakago-sha''' (中五社) * {{ill|Suwa Shrine (Tokushima)|ja|諏訪神社 (徳島市)}} - Minami-Sako 3-chome * {{ill|Shisho Shrine (Tokushima)|ja|四所神社 (徳島市)}} - Fukushima, Tokushima * {{ill|Hachiman Shrine (Tokushima)|ja|八幡神社 (徳島市)}} - Iga-cho, Tokushima * {{ill|Kotohira Shrine (Tokushima)|ja|金刀比羅神社 (徳島市)}} - Semimachi, Tokushima

{{otheruses|Shinto shrines in Myozan, Tokushima City, Tokushima Prefecture|a shrine in Shimosuketo, Tokushima City|Kasuga Shrine (Shimosuketo, Tokushima)}} {{Infobox Shinto shrine | name = Kasuga Shrine (春日神社) | religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]] |image = [[File:Kasuga Jinjya.jpeg|250px]] | location = {{ill|Myozan, Tokushima City|ja|眉山町}}, {{ill|Tokushima Prefecture|ja|徳島県}}, Japan | coordinates = {{Coord|34|04|19.9|N|134|32|33.4|E|scale:25000|display=inline,title}} | deity = {{ill|Takemikazuchi|ja|武甕槌命}}, {{ill|Izanagi-no-Mikoto|ja|斎主命}}, {{ill|Amenokoyane no Mikoto|ja|天児屋根命}}, {{ill|Hime no Kami|ja|比売神}} | rank = Former {{ill|Ken-sha|ja|県社}} | founded = 1586 (Tenshō 14) | main_building = {{ill|Kasuga-zukuri|ja|春日造}} | festivals = {{ill|April 17|ja|4月17日}}, {{ill|October 17|ja|10月17日}} }}
[[File:Kasugasui.jpeg|thumb|250px|right|Kasuga Spring (春日水)]] '''Kasuga Shrine''' (春日神社) is a {{ill|Shinto shrine|ja|神社}} located in {{ill|Myozan, Tokushima City|ja|眉山町}}, {{ill|Tokushima Prefecture|ja|徳島県}}, Japan. It is situated on the eastern foothills of {{ill|Mount Bizan|ja|眉山}}.
== Deities == The shrine enshrines the following four {{ill|Kami|ja|柱}} (deities), identical to those of {{ill|Kasuga Taisha|ja|春日大社|1=Kasuga-taisha}} in {{ill|Nara Prefecture|ja|奈良県}}: * {{ill|Takemikazuchi|ja|武甕槌命}} * {{ill|Izanagi-no-Mikoto|ja|斎主命}} * {{ill|Amenokoyane no Mikoto|ja|天児屋根命}} * {{ill|Hime no Kami|ja|比売神}}
== History == The shrine traces its origins to a {{ill|Kasuga Shrine|ja|春日祠}} enshrined at the Kasuga territory in {{ill|Tomi-da|ja|富田庄}} (modern {{ill|Irida|ja|入田町}}, Tokushima City), a former estate of Kasuga Shrine in {{ill|Yamato Province|ja|Yamato Province }}. It is said to have been relocated to its current site at Otakiyama during the transfer of power to the {{ill|Hachisuka clan|ja|蜂須賀氏}} in 1586, coinciding with the construction of {{ill|Tokushima Castle|ja|徳島城}}. Another account suggests the shrine was moved from {{ill|Tamiya Village|ja|田宮村}} along with Shofuku-ji Temple, which later became the shrine’s {{ill|Bettōji|ja|別当寺}} before its abolition in the early {{ill|Meiji period|ja|明治時代}}.<ref>According to the ''Awa-shi'' (阿波志), compiled in 1815.</ref>
During the {{ill|Keicho era|ja|慶長}} (late 16th to early 17th century), the shrine was referred to as "Kasuga Daimyōjin" and received significant patronage from the Hachisuka clan, including an annual offering of 10 koku of rice. In 1873, it was officially renamed Kasuga Shrine and designated as a {{ill|Ken-sha|ja|県社}}. The shrine also features "Kasuga Spring" (春日水), one of the notable {{ill|Mount Bizan springs|ja|眉山湧水群}}.
== Sub-Shrines == The shrine complex includes the following sub-shrines: * '''Toyotama-hime Shrine''' (deity: {{ill|Toyotama-hime|ja|豊玉比賣}}) * Enshrines the deity formerly worshipped at Ryuo Shrine within Tokushima Castle. * '''Wakamiya Shrine''' (deity: {{ill|Ame-no-Kumunushi|ja|天忍雲根命}}) * '''Akiba Shrine''' (deity: {{ill|Amaterasu|ja|天照大御神}}, {{ill|Onamuchi|ja|大巳貴命}}, {{ill|Haniyasubime|ja|埴安姫神}}, {{ill|Ukemochi|ja|保食神}}, {{ill|Sukunabikona|ja|少彦名命}})
== Transportation == * '''By car''': 5 minutes from {{ill|Tokushima Station|ja|徳島駅}}, {{ill|Shikoku Railway Company|ja|四国旅客鉄道}} (JR Shikoku).
== References == {{reflist}}
== Related Shrines == * '''Tokushima City Nakago-sha''' (中五社) * {{ill|Suwa Shrine (Tokushima)|ja|諏訪神社 (徳島市)}} - Minami-Sako 3-chome * {{ill|Shisho Shrine (Tokushima)|ja|四所神社 (徳島市)}} - Fukushima, Tokushima * {{ill|Hachiman Shrine (Tokushima)|ja|八幡神社 (徳島市)}} - Iga-cho, Tokushima * {{ill|Kotohira Shrine (Tokushima)|ja|金刀比羅神社 (徳島市)}} - Semimachi, Tokushima

== Deities == The shrine enshrines the following four {{ill|Kami|ja|柱}} (deities), identical to those of {{ill|Kasuga Taisha|ja|春日大社|1=Kasuga-taisha}} in {{ill|Nara Prefecture|ja|奈良県}}: * {{ill|Takemikazuchi|ja|武甕槌命}} * {{ill|Izanagi-no-Mikoto|ja|斎主命}} * {{ill|Amenokoyane no Mikoto|ja|天児屋根命|1=Ame-no-Koyane}} * {{ill|Hime no Kami|ja|比売神}}
== History == The shrine traces its origins to a {{ill|Kasuga Shrine|ja|春日祠}} enshrined at the Kasuga territory in {{ill|Tomi-da|ja|富田庄}} (modern {{ill|Irida|ja|入田町}}, Tokushima City), a former estate of Kasuga Shrine in {{ill|Yamato Province|ja|Yamato Province }}. It is said to have been relocated to its current site at Otakiyama during the transfer of power to the {{ill|Hachisuka clan|ja|蜂須賀氏}} in 1586, coinciding with the construction of {{ill|Tokushima Castle|ja|徳島城}}. Another account suggests the shrine was moved from {{ill|Tamiya Village|ja|田宮村}} along with Shofuku-ji Temple, which later became the shrine’s {{ill|Bettōji|ja|別当寺}} before its abolition in the early {{ill|Meiji period|ja|明治時代}}.<ref>According to the ''Awa-shi'' (阿波志), compiled in 1815.</ref>
During the {{ill|Keicho era|ja|慶長}} (late 16th to early 17th century), the shrine was referred to as "Kasuga Daimyōjin" and received significant patronage from the Hachisuka clan, including an annual offering of 10 koku of rice. In 1873, it was officially renamed Kasuga Shrine and designated as a {{ill|Ken-sha|ja|県社}}. The shrine also features "Kasuga Spring" (春日水), one of the notable {{ill|Mount Bizan springs|ja|眉山湧水群}}.
== Sub-Shrines == The shrine complex includes the following sub-shrines: * '''Toyotama-hime Shrine''' (deity: {{ill|Toyotama-hime|ja|豊玉比賣}}) * Enshrines the deity formerly worshipped at Ryuo Shrine within Tokushima Castle. * '''Wakamiya Shrine''' (deity: {{ill|Ame-no-Kumunushi|ja|天忍雲根命}}) * '''Akiba Shrine''' (deity: {{ill|Amaterasu|ja|天照大御神}}, {{ill|Onamuchi|ja|大巳貴命}}, {{ill|Haniyasubime|ja|埴安姫神}}, {{ill|Ukemochi|ja|保食神}}, {{ill|Sukunabikona|ja|少彦名命}})
== Transportation == * '''By car''': 5 minutes from {{ill|Tokushima Station|ja|徳島駅}}, {{ill|Shikoku Railway Company|ja|四国旅客鉄道}} (JR Shikoku).

{{otheruses|Shinto shrines in Myozan, Tokushima City, Tokushima Prefecture|a shrine in Shimosuketo, Tokushima City|Kasuga Shrine (Shimosuketo, Tokushima)}} {{Infobox Shinto shrine | name = Kasuga Shrine (春日神社) | religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]] |image = [[File:Kasuga Jinjya.jpeg|250px]] | location = {{ill|Myozan, Tokushima City|ja|眉山町}}, {{ill|Tokushima Prefecture|ja|徳島県}}, Japan | coordinates = {{Coord|34|04|19.9|N|134|32|33.4|E|scale:25000|display=inline,title}} | deity = {{ill|Takemikazuchi|ja|武甕槌命}}, {{ill|Izanagi-no-Mikoto|ja|斎主命}}, {{ill|Amenokoyane no Mikoto|ja|天児屋根命|1=Ame-no-Koyane}}, {{ill|Hime no Kami|ja|比売神}} | rank = Former {{ill|Ken-sha|ja|県社}} | founded = 1586 (Tenshō 14) | main_building = {{ill|Kasuga-zukuri|ja|春日造}} | festivals = {{ill|April 17|ja|4月17日}}, {{ill|October 17|ja|10月17日}} }}
[[File:Kasugasui.jpeg|thumb|250px|right|Kasuga Spring (春日水)]] '''Kasuga Shrine''' (春日神社) is a {{ill|Shinto shrine|ja|神社}} located in {{ill|Myozan, Tokushima City|ja|眉山町}}, {{ill|Tokushima Prefecture|ja|徳島県}}, Japan. It is situated on the eastern foothills of {{ill|Mount Bizan|ja|眉山}}.
== Deities == The shrine enshrines the following four {{ill|Kami|ja|柱}} (deities), identical to those of {{ill|Kasuga Taisha|ja|春日大社|1=Kasuga-taisha}} in {{ill|Nara Prefecture|ja|奈良県}}: * {{ill|Takemikazuchi|ja|武甕槌命}} * {{ill|Izanagi-no-Mikoto|ja|斎主命}} * {{ill|Amenokoyane no Mikoto|ja|天児屋根命|1=Ame-no-Koyane}} * {{ill|Hime no Kami|ja|比売神}}
== History == The shrine traces its origins to a {{ill|Kasuga Shrine|ja|春日祠}} enshrined at the Kasuga territory in {{ill|Tomi-da|ja|富田庄}} (modern {{ill|Irida|ja|入田町}}, Tokushima City), a former estate of Kasuga Shrine in {{ill|Yamato Province|ja|Yamato Province }}. It is said to have been relocated to its current site at Otakiyama during the transfer of power to the {{ill|Hachisuka clan|ja|蜂須賀氏}} in 1586, coinciding with the construction of {{ill|Tokushima Castle|ja|徳島城}}. Another account suggests the shrine was moved from {{ill|Tamiya Village|ja|田宮村}} along with Shofuku-ji Temple, which later became the shrine’s {{ill|Bettōji|ja|別当寺}} before its abolition in the early {{ill|Meiji period|ja|明治時代}}.<ref>According to the ''Awa-shi'' (阿波志), compiled in 1815.</ref>
During the {{ill|Keicho era|ja|慶長}} (late 16th to early 17th century), the shrine was referred to as "Kasuga Daimyōjin" and received significant patronage from the Hachisuka clan, including an annual offering of 10 koku of rice. In 1873, it was officially renamed Kasuga Shrine and designated as a {{ill|Ken-sha|ja|県社}}. The shrine also features "Kasuga Spring" (春日水), one of the notable {{ill|Mount Bizan springs|ja|眉山湧水群}}.
== Sub-Shrines == The shrine complex includes the following sub-shrines: * '''Toyotama-hime Shrine''' (deity: {{ill|Toyotama-hime|ja|豊玉比賣}}) ** Enshrines the deity formerly worshipped at Ryuo Shrine within Tokushima Castle. * '''Wakamiya Shrine''' (deity: {{ill|Ame-no-Kumunushi|ja|天忍雲根命}}) * '''Akiba Shrine''' (deity: {{ill|Amaterasu|ja|天照大御神}}, {{ill|Onamuchi|ja|大巳貴命}}, {{ill|Haniyasubime|ja|埴安姫神}}, {{ill|Ukemochi|ja|保食神}}, {{ill|Sukunabikona|ja|少彦名命}})
== Transportation == * '''By car''': 5 minutes from {{ill|Tokushima Station|ja|徳島駅}}, {{ill|Shikoku Railway Company|ja|四国旅客鉄道}} (JR Shikoku).
== References == {{reflist}}
== Related Shrines == * '''Tokushima City Nakago-sha''' (中五社) ** {{ill|Suwa Shrine (Tokushima)|ja|諏訪神社 (徳島市)}} - Minami-Sako 3-chome ** {{ill|Shisho Shrine (Tokushima)|ja|四所神社 (徳島市)}} - Fukushima, Tokushima ** {{ill|Hachiman Shrine (Tokushima)|ja|八幡神社 (徳島市)}} - Iga-cho, Tokushima ** {{ill|Kotohira Shrine (Tokushima)|ja|金刀比羅神社 (徳島市)}} - Semimachi, Tokushima

== History == The shrine traces its origins to a {{ill|Kasuga Shrine|ja|春日祠}} enshrined at the Kasuga territory in {{ill|Tomi-da|ja|富田庄}} (modern {{ill|Irida|ja|入田町}}, Tokushima City), a former estate of Kasuga Shrine in {{ill|Yamato Province|ja|Yamato Province }}. It is said to have been relocated to its current site at Otakiyama during the transfer of power to the {{ill|Hachisuka clan|ja|蜂須賀氏}} in 1586, coinciding with the construction of {{ill|Tokushima Castle|ja|徳島城}}. Another account suggests the shrine was moved from {{ill|Tamiya Village|ja|田宮村}} along with Shofuku-ji Temple, which later became the shrine’s {{ill|Bettōji|ja|別当寺}} before its abolition in the early {{ill|Meiji period|ja|明治時代}}.<ref>According to the ''Awa-shi'' (阿波志), compiled in 1815.</ref>
During the {{ill|Keicho era|ja|慶長}} (late 16th to early 17th century), the shrine was referred to as "Kasuga Daimyōjin" and received significant patronage from the Hachisuka clan, including an annual offering of 10 koku of rice. In 1873, it was officially renamed Kasuga Shrine and designated as a {{ill|Ken-sha|ja|県社}}. The shrine also features "Kasuga Spring" (春日水), one of the notable {{ill|Mount Bizan springs|ja|眉山湧水群}}.
== Sub-Shrines == The shrine complex includes the following sub-shrines: * '''Toyotama-hime Shrine''' (deity: {{ill|Toyotama-hime|ja|豊玉比賣}}) ** Enshrines the deity formerly worshipped at Ryuo Shrine within Tokushima Castle. * '''Wakamiya Shrine''' (deity: {{ill|Ame-no-Kumunushi|ja|天忍雲根命}}) * '''Akiba Shrine''' (deity: {{ill|Amaterasu|ja|天照大御神}}, {{ill|Onamuchi|ja|大巳貴命}}, {{ill|Haniyasubime|ja|埴安姫神}}, {{ill|Ukemochi|ja|保食神}}, {{ill|Sukunabikona|ja|少彦名命}})
== Transportation == * '''By car''': 5 minutes from {{ill|Tokushima Station|ja|徳島駅}}, {{ill|Shikoku Railway Company|ja|四国旅客鉄道}} (JR Shikoku).

{{otheruses|Shinto shrines in Myozan, Tokushima City, Tokushima Prefecture|a shrine in Shimosuketo, Tokushima City|Kasuga Shrine (Shimosuketo, Tokushima)}} {{Infobox Shinto shrine | name = Kasuga Shrine (春日神社) | religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]] |image = [[File:Kasuga Jinjya.jpeg|250px]] | location = {{ill|Myozan, Tokushima City|ja|眉山町}}, {{ill|Tokushima Prefecture|ja|徳島県}}, Japan | coordinates = {{Coord|34|04|19.9|N|134|32|33.4|E|scale:25000|display=inline,title}} | deity = {{ill|Takemikazuchi|ja|武甕槌命}}, {{ill|Izanagi-no-Mikoto|ja|斎主命}}, {{ill|Amenokoyane no Mikoto|ja|天児屋根命|1=Ame-no-Koyane}}, {{ill|Hime no Kami|ja|比売神}} | rank = Former {{ill|Ken-sha|ja|県社}} | founded = 1586 (Tenshō 14) | main_building = {{ill|Kasuga-zukuri|ja|春日造}} | festivals = {{ill|April 17|ja|4月17日}}, {{ill|October 17|ja|10月17日}} }}
[[File:Kasugasui.jpeg|thumb|250px|right|Kasuga Spring (春日水)]] '''Kasuga Shrine''' (春日神社) is a {{ill|Shinto shrine|ja|神社}} located in {{ill|Myozan, Tokushima City|ja|眉山町}}, {{ill|Tokushima Prefecture|ja|徳島県}}, Japan. It is situated on the eastern foothills of {{ill|Mount Bizan|ja|眉山}}.
== Deities == The shrine enshrines the following four {{ill|Kami|ja|柱}} (deities), identical to those of {{ill|Kasuga Taisha|ja|春日大社|1=Kasuga-taisha}} in {{ill|Nara Prefecture|ja|奈良県}}: * {{ill|Takemikazuchi|ja|武甕槌命}} * {{ill|Izanagi-no-Mikoto|ja|斎主命}} * {{ill|Amenokoyane no Mikoto|ja|天児屋根命|1=Ame-no-Koyane}} * {{ill|Hime no Kami|ja|比売神}}
== History == The shrine traces its origins to a {{ill|Kasuga Shrine|ja|春日祠}} enshrined at the Kasuga territory in {{ill|Tomi-da|ja|富田庄}} (modern {{ill|Irida|ja|入田町}}, Tokushima City), a former estate of Kasuga Shrine in {{ill|Yamato Province|ja|Yamato Province }}. It is said to have been relocated to its current site at Otakiyama during the transfer of power to the {{ill|Hachisuka clan|ja|蜂須賀氏}} in 1586, coinciding with the construction of {{ill|Tokushima Castle|ja|徳島城}}. Another account suggests the shrine was moved from {{ill|Tamiya Village|ja|田宮村}} along with Shofuku-ji Temple, which later became the shrine’s {{ill|Bettōji|ja|別当寺}} before its abolition in the early {{ill|Meiji period|ja|明治時代}}.<ref>According to the ''Awa-shi'' (阿波志), compiled in 1815.</ref>
During the {{ill|Keicho era|ja|慶長}} (late 16th to early 17th century), the shrine was referred to as "Kasuga Daimyōjin" and received significant patronage from the Hachisuka clan, including an annual offering of 10 koku of rice. In 1873, it was officially renamed Kasuga Shrine and designated as a {{ill|Ken-sha|ja|県社}}. The shrine also features "Kasuga Spring" (春日水), one of the notable {{ill|Mount Bizan springs|ja|眉山湧水群}}.
== Sub-Shrines == The shrine complex includes the following sub-shrines: * '''Toyotama-hime Shrine''' (deity: {{ill|Toyotama-hime|ja|豊玉比賣}}) ** Enshrines the deity formerly worshipped at Ryuo Shrine within Tokushima Castle. * '''Wakamiya Shrine''' (deity: {{ill|Ame-no-Kumunushi|ja|天忍雲根命}}) * '''Akiba Shrine''' (deity: {{ill|Amaterasu|ja|天照大御神}}, {{ill|Onamuchi|ja|大巳貴命}}, {{ill|Haniyasubime|ja|埴安姫神}}, {{ill|Ukemochi|ja|保食神}}, {{ill|Sukunabikona|ja|少彦名命}})
== Transportation == * '''By car''': 5 minutes from {{ill|Tokushima Station|ja|徳島駅}}, {{ill|Shikoku Railway Company|ja|四国旅客鉄道}} (JR Shikoku).
== References == {{reflist}}
== Related Shrines == * '''Tokushima City Nakago-sha''' (中五社) ** {{ill|Suwa Shrine (Tokushima City)|ja|諏訪神社 (徳島市)}} - Minami-Sako 3-chome ** {{ill|Shisho Shrine (Tokushima)|ja|四所神社 (徳島市)}} - Fukushima, Tokushima ** {{ill|Hachiman Shrine (Tokushima)|ja|八幡神社 (徳島市)}} - Iga-cho, Tokushima ** {{ill|Kotohira Shrine (Tokushima)|ja|金刀比羅神社 (徳島市)}} - Semimachi, Tokushima

== History == The shrine traces its origins to a {{ill|Kasuga Shrine|ja|春日祠}} enshrined at the Kasuga territory in {{ill|Tomi-da|ja|富田庄}} (modern {{ill|Irida|ja|入田町}}, Tokushima City), a former estate of Kasuga Shrine in {{ill|Yamato Province|ja|Yamato Province }}. It is said to have been relocated to its current site at Otakiyama during the transfer of power to the {{ill|Hachisuka clan|ja|蜂須賀氏}} in 1586, coinciding with the construction of {{ill|Tokushima Castle|ja|徳島城}}. Another account suggests the shrine was moved from {{ill|Tamiya Village|ja|田宮村}} along with Shofuku-ji Temple, which later became the shrine’s {{ill|Bettōji|ja|別当寺}} before its abolition in the early {{ill|Meiji period|ja|明治時代}}.<ref>According to the ''Awa-shi'' (阿波志), compiled in 1815.</ref>
During the {{ill|Keicho era|ja|慶長}} (late 16th to early 17th century), the shrine was referred to as "Kasuga Daimyōjin" and received significant patronage from the Hachisuka clan, including an annual offering of 10 koku of rice. In 1873, it was officially renamed Kasuga Shrine and designated as a {{ill|Ken-sha|ja|県社}}. The shrine also features "Kasuga Spring" (春日水), one of the notable {{ill|Mount Bizan springs|ja|眉山湧水群}}.

{{otheruses|Shinto shrines in Myozan, Tokushima City, Tokushima Prefecture|a shrine in Shimosuketo, Tokushima City|Kasuga Shrine (Shimosuketo, Tokushima)}} {{Infobox Shinto shrine | name = Kasuga Shrine (春日神社) | religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]] |image = [[File:Kasuga Jinjya.jpeg|250px]] | location = {{ill|Myozan, Tokushima City|ja|眉山町}}, {{ill|Tokushima Prefecture|ja|徳島県}}, Japan | coordinates = {{Coord|34|04|19.9|N|134|32|33.4|E|scale:25000|display=inline,title}} | deity = {{ill|Takemikazuchi|ja|武甕槌命}}, {{ill|Izanagi-no-Mikoto|ja|斎主命}}, {{ill|Amenokoyane no Mikoto|ja|天児屋根命|1=Ame-no-Koyane}}, {{ill|Hime no Kami|ja|比売神}} | rank = Former {{ill|Ken-sha|ja|県社}} | founded = 1586 (Tenshō 14) | main_building = {{ill|Kasuga-zukuri|ja|春日造}} | festivals = {{ill|April 17|ja|4月17日}}, {{ill|October 17|ja|10月17日}} }}
[[File:Kasugasui.jpeg|thumb|250px|right|Kasuga Spring (春日水)]] '''Kasuga Shrine''' (春日神社) is a {{ill|Shinto shrine|ja|神社}} located in {{ill|Myozan, Tokushima City|ja|眉山町}}, {{ill|Tokushima Prefecture|ja|徳島県}}, Japan. It is situated on the eastern foothills of {{ill|Mount Bizan|ja|眉山}}.
== Deities == The shrine enshrines the following four {{ill|Kami|ja|柱}} (deities), identical to those of {{ill|Kasuga Taisha|ja|春日大社|1=Kasuga-taisha}} in {{ill|Nara Prefecture|ja|奈良県}}: * {{ill|Takemikazuchi|ja|武甕槌命}} * {{ill|Izanagi-no-Mikoto|ja|斎主命}} * {{ill|Amenokoyane no Mikoto|ja|天児屋根命|1=Ame-no-Koyane}} * {{ill|Hime no Kami|ja|比売神}}
== History == The shrine traces its origins to a {{ill|Kasuga Shrine|ja|春日祠}} enshrined at the Kasuga territory in {{ill|Tomi-da|ja|富田庄}} (modern {{ill|Irida|ja|入田町}}, Tokushima City), a former estate of Kasuga Shrine in {{ill|Yamato Province|ja|Yamato Province }}. It is said to have been relocated to its current site at Otakiyama during the transfer of power to the {{ill|Hachisuka clan|ja|蜂須賀氏}} in 1586, coinciding with the construction of {{ill|Tokushima Castle|ja|徳島城}}. Another account suggests the shrine was moved from {{ill|Tamiya Village|ja|田宮村}} along with Shofuku-ji Temple, which later became the shrine’s {{ill|Bettōji|ja|別当寺}} before its abolition in the early {{ill|Meiji period|ja|明治時代}}.<ref>According to the ''Awa-shi'' (阿波志), compiled in 1815.</ref>
During the {{ill|Keicho era|ja|慶長}} (late 16th to early 17th century), the shrine was referred to as "Kasuga Daimyōjin" and received significant patronage from the Hachisuka clan, including an annual offering of 10 koku of rice. In 1873, it was officially renamed Kasuga Shrine and designated as a {{ill|Ken-sha|ja|県社}}. The shrine also features "Kasuga Spring" (春日水), one of the notable {{ill|Mount Bizan springs|ja|眉山湧水群}}.
== Sub-Shrines == The shrine complex includes the following sub-shrines: * '''Toyotama-hime Shrine''' (deity: {{ill|Toyotama-hime|ja|豊玉比賣}}) ** Enshrines the deity formerly worshipped at Ryuo Shrine within Tokushima Castle. * '''Wakamiya Shrine''' (deity: {{ill|Ame-no-Kumunushi|ja|天忍雲根命}}) * '''Akiba Shrine''' (deity: {{ill|Amaterasu|ja|天照大御神}}, {{ill|Onamuchi|ja|大巳貴命}}, {{ill|Haniyasubime|ja|埴安姫神}}, {{ill|Ukemochi|ja|保食神}}, {{ill|Sukunabikona|ja|少彦名命|1=Sukunabikona}})
== Transportation == * '''By car''': 5 minutes from {{ill|Tokushima Station|ja|徳島駅}}, {{ill|Shikoku Railway Company|ja|四国旅客鉄道}} (JR Shikoku).
== References == {{reflist}}
== Related Shrines == * '''Tokushima City Nakago-sha''' (中五社) ** {{ill|Suwa Shrine (Tokushima City)|ja|諏訪神社 (徳島市)}} - Minami-Sako 3-chome ** {{ill|Shisho Shrine (Tokushima)|ja|四所神社 (徳島市)}} - Fukushima, Tokushima ** {{ill|Hachiman Shrine (Tokushima)|ja|八幡神社 (徳島市)}} - Iga-cho, Tokushima ** {{ill|Kotohira Shrine (Tokushima)|ja|金刀比羅神社 (徳島市)}} - Semimachi, Tokushima

[[File:Kasugasui.jpeg|thumb|250px|right|Kasuga Spring (春日水)]] '''Kasuga Shrine''' (春日神社) is a {{ill|Shinto shrine|ja|神社|12=draft|12=draft}} located in {{ill|Myozan, Tokushima City|ja|眉山町|12=draft|12=draft}}, {{ill|Tokushima Prefecture|ja|徳島県|12=draft|12=draft}}, Japan. It is situated on the eastern foothills of {{ill|Mount Bizan|ja|眉山|12=draft|12=draft}}.
== Deities == The shrine enshrines the following four {{ill|Kami|ja|柱|12=draft|12=draft}} (deities), identical to those of {{ill|Kasuga Taisha|ja|春日大社|1=Kasuga-taisha|12=draft|12=draft}} in {{ill|Nara Prefecture|ja|奈良県|12=draft|12=draft}}: * {{ill|Takemikazuchi|ja|武甕槌命|12=draft|12=draft}} * {{ill|Izanagi-no-Mikoto|ja|斎主命|12=draft|12=draft}} * {{ill|Amenokoyane no Mikoto|ja|天児屋根命|1=Ame-no-Koyane|12=draft|12=draft}} * {{ill|Hime no Kami|ja|比売神|12=draft|12=draft}}
== History == The shrine traces its origins to a {{ill|Kasuga Shrine|ja|春日祠|12=draft|12=draft}} enshrined at the Kasuga territory in {{ill|Tomi-da|ja|富田庄|12=draft|12=draft}} (modern {{ill|Irida|ja|入田町|12=draft|12=draft}}, Tokushima City), a former estate of Kasuga Shrine in {{ill|Yamato Province|ja|Yamato Province|12=draft|12=draft}}. It is said to have been relocated to its current site at Otakiyama during the transfer of power to the {{ill|Hachisuka clan|ja|蜂須賀氏|12=draft|12=draft}} in 1586, coinciding with the construction of {{ill|Tokushima Castle|ja|徳島城|12=draft|12=draft}}. Another account suggests the shrine was moved from {{ill|Tamiya Village|ja|田宮村|12=draft|12=draft}} along with Shofuku-ji Temple, which later became the shrine’s {{ill|Bettōji|ja|別当寺|12=draft|12=draft}} before its abolition in the early {{ill|Meiji period|ja|明治時代|12=draft|12=draft}}.<ref>According to the ''Awa-shi'' (阿波志), compiled in 1815.</ref>
During the {{ill|Keicho era|ja|慶長|12=draft|12=draft}} (late 16th to early 17th century), the shrine was referred to as "Kasuga Daimyōjin" and received significant patronage from the Hachisuka clan, including an annual offering of 10 koku of rice. In 1873, it was officially renamed Kasuga Shrine and designated as a {{ill|Ken-sha|ja|県社|12=draft|12=draft}}. The shrine also features "Kasuga Spring" (春日水), one of the notable {{ill|Mount Bizan springs|ja|眉山湧水群|12=draft|12=draft}}.
== Sub-Shrines == The shrine complex includes the following sub-shrines: * '''Toyotama-hime Shrine''' (deity: {{ill|Toyotama-hime|ja|豊玉比賣|12=draft|12=draft}}) ** Enshrines the deity formerly worshipped at Ryuo Shrine within Tokushima Castle. * '''Wakamiya Shrine''' (deity: {{ill|Ame-no-Kumunushi|ja|天忍雲根命|12=draft|12=draft}}) * '''Akiba Shrine''' (deity: {{ill|Amaterasu|ja|天照大御神|12=draft|12=draft}}, {{ill|Onamuchi|ja|大巳貴命|12=draft|12=draft}}, {{ill|Haniyasubime|ja|埴安姫神|12=draft|12=draft}}, {{ill|Ukemochi|ja|保食神|12=draft|12=draft}}, {{ill|Sukunabikona|ja|少彦名命|1=Sukunabikona|12=draft|12=draft}})
== Transportation == * '''By car''': 5 minutes from {{ill|Tokushima Station|ja|徳島駅|12=draft|12=draft}}, {{ill|Shikoku Railway Company|ja|四国旅客鉄道|12=draft|12=draft}} (JR Shikoku).
== References == {{reflist}}
== Related Shrines == * '''Tokushima City Nakago-sha''' (中五社) ** {{ill|Suwa Shrine (Tokushima City)|ja|諏訪神社 (徳島市)|12=draft|12=draft}} - Minami-Sako 3-chome ** {{ill|Shisho Shrine (Tokushima)|ja|四所神社 (徳島市)|12=draft|12=draft}} - Fukushima, Tokushima ** {{ill|Hachiman Shrine (Tokushima)|ja|八幡神社 (徳島市)|12=draft|12=draft}} - Iga-cho, Tokushima ** {{ill|Kotohira Shrine (Tokushima)|ja|金刀比羅神社 (徳島市)|12=draft|12=draft}} - Semimachi, Tokushima

{{otheruses|Shinto shrines in Myozan, Tokushima City, Tokushima Prefecture|a shrine in Shimosuketo, Tokushima City|Kasuga Shrine (Shimosuketo, Tokushima)}} {{Infobox Shinto shrine | name = Kasuga Shrine (春日神社) | religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]] |image = [[File:Kasuga Jinjya.jpeg|250px]] | location = {{ill|Myozan, Tokushima City|ja|眉山町|12=draft|12=draft}}, {{ill|Tokushima Prefecture|ja|徳島県|12=draft|12=draft}}, Japan | coordinates = {{Coord|34|04|19.9|N|134|32|33.4|E|scale:25000|display=inline,title}} | deity = {{ill|Takemikazuchi|ja|武甕槌命|12=draft|12=draft}}, {{ill|Izanagi-no-Mikoto|ja|斎主命|12=draft|12=draft}}, {{ill|Amenokoyane no Mikoto|ja|天児屋根命|1=Ame-no-Koyane|12=draft|12=draft}}, {{ill|Hime no Kami|ja|比売神|12=draft|12=draft}} | rank = Former {{ill|Ken-sha|ja|県社|12=draft|12=draft}} | founded = 1586 (Tenshō 14) | main_building = {{ill|Kasuga-zukuri|ja|春日造|12=draft|12=draft}} | festivals = {{ill|April 17|ja|4月17日|12=draft|12=draft}}, {{ill|October 17|ja|10月17日|12=draft|12=draft}} }}
[[File:Kasugasui.jpeg|thumb|250px|right|Kasuga Spring (春日水)]] '''Kasuga Shrine''' (春日神社) is a {{ill|Shinto shrine|ja|神社|12=draft|12=draft}} located in {{ill|Myozan, Tokushima City|ja|眉山町|12=draft|12=draft}}, {{ill|Tokushima Prefecture|ja|徳島県|12=draft|12=draft}}, Japan. It is situated on the eastern foothills of {{ill|Mount Bizan|ja|眉山|12=draft|12=draft}}.
== Deities == The shrine enshrines the following four {{ill|Kami|ja|柱|12=draft|12=draft}} (deities), identical to those of {{ill|Kasuga Taisha|ja|春日大社|1=Kasuga-taisha|12=draft|12=draft}} in {{ill|Nara Prefecture|ja|奈良県|12=draft|12=draft}}: * {{ill|Takemikazuchi|ja|武甕槌命|12=draft|12=draft}} * {{ill|Izanagi-no-Mikoto|ja|斎主命|12=draft|12=draft}} * {{ill|Amenokoyane no Mikoto|ja|天児屋根命|1=Ame-no-Koyane|12=draft|12=draft}} * {{ill|Hime no Kami|ja|比売神|12=draft|12=draft}}
== History == The shrine traces its origins to a {{ill|Kasuga Shrine|ja|春日祠|12=draft|12=draft}} enshrined at the Kasuga territory in {{ill|Tomi-da|ja|富田庄|12=draft|12=draft}} (modern {{ill|Irida|ja|入田町|12=draft|12=draft}}, Tokushima City), a former estate of Kasuga Shrine in {{ill|Yamato Province|ja|Yamato Province|12=draft|12=draft}}. It is said to have been relocated to its current site at Otakiyama during the transfer of power to the {{ill|Hachisuka clan|ja|蜂須賀氏|12=draft|12=draft}} in 1586, coinciding with the construction of {{ill|Tokushima Castle|ja|徳島城|12=draft|12=draft}}. Another account suggests the shrine was moved from {{ill|Tamiya Village|ja|田宮村|12=draft|12=draft}} along with Shofuku-ji Temple, which later became the shrine’s {{ill|Bettōji|ja|別当寺|12=draft|12=draft}} before its abolition in the early {{ill|Meiji period|ja|明治時代|12=draft|12=draft}}.<ref>According to the ''Awa-shi'' (阿波志), compiled in 1815.</ref>
During the {{ill|Keicho era|ja|慶長|12=draft|12=draft}} (late 16th to early 17th century), the shrine was referred to as "Kasuga Daimyōjin" and received significant patronage from the Hachisuka clan, including an annual offering of 10 koku of rice. In 1873, it was officially renamed Kasuga Shrine and designated as a {{ill|Ken-sha|ja|県社|12=draft|12=draft}}. The shrine also features "Kasuga Spring" (春日水), one of the notable {{ill|Mount Bizan springs|ja|眉山湧水群|12=draft|12=draft}}.
== Sub-Shrines == The shrine complex includes the following sub-shrines: * '''Toyotama-hime Shrine''' (deity: {{ill|Toyotama-hime|ja|豊玉比賣|12=draft|12=draft}}) ** Enshrines the deity formerly worshipped at Ryuo Shrine within Tokushima Castle. * '''Wakamiya Shrine''' (deity: {{ill|Ame-no-Kumunushi|ja|天忍雲根命|12=draft|12=draft}}) * '''Akiba Shrine''' (deity: {{ill|Amaterasu|ja|天照大御神|12=draft|12=draft}}, {{ill|Onamuchi|ja|大巳貴命|12=draft|12=draft}}, {{ill|Haniyasubime|ja|埴安姫神|12=draft|12=draft}}, {{ill|Ukemochi|ja|保食神|12=draft|12=draft}}, {{ill|Sukunabikona|ja|少彦名命|1=Sukunabikona|12=draft|12=draft}})
== Transportation == * '''By car''': 5 minutes from {{ill|Tokushima Station|ja|徳島駅|12=draft|12=draft}}, {{ill|Shikoku Railway Company|ja|四国旅客鉄道|12=draft|12=draft}} (JR Shikoku).
== References == {{reflist}}
== Related Shrines == * '''Tokushima City Nakago-sha''' (中五社) ** {{ill|Suwa Shrine (Tokushima City)|ja|諏訪神社 (徳島市)|12=draft|12=draft}} - Minami-Sako 3-chome ** {{ill|Shisho Shrine (Tokushima)|ja|四所神社 (徳島市)|12=draft|12=draft}} - Fukushima, Tokushima ** {{ill|Hachiman Shrine (Tokushima)|ja|八幡神社 (徳島市)|12=draft|12=draft}} - Iga-cho, Tokushima ** {{ill|Kotohira Shrine (Tokushima)|ja|金刀比羅神社 (徳島市)|12=draft|12=draft}} - Semimachi, Tokushima

{{otheruses|徳島県徳島市眉山町の神社|徳島県徳島市下助任町の神社|春日神社 (徳島市下助任町)}} {{神社 |名称 = 春日神社 |画像 = [[ファイル:Kasuga Jinjya.jpeg|250px]] |所在地 = [[徳島県]][[徳島市]][[眉山町]]大滝山1 |位置 = {{ウィキ座標2段度分秒|34|04|19.9|N|134|32|33.4|E|scale:25000|display=inline,title}} |祭神 = [[武甕槌命]]、[[斎主命]]、[[天児屋根命]]、[[比売神]] |社格 = 旧県社 |創建 = 天正14年（1586年） |別名 = |札所等 = 徳島市中五社 |本殿 = [[春日造]] |例祭 = [[4月17日]]、[[10月17日]] |神事 = }} [[ファイル:Kasugasui.jpeg|thumb|250px|right|春日水]] '''春日神社'''（かすがじんじゃ）は、[[徳島県]][[徳島市]][[眉山町]]にある[[神社]]である。[[眉山 (徳島市)|眉山]]東麓の大滝山に位置する。
== 祭神 == [[武甕槌命]]、[[斎主命]]、[[天児屋根命]]、[[比売神]]の4[[柱]]で、[[奈良県]]の[[春日大社]]と同じ神々を祀っている。
== 歴史 == [[大和国]]春日社領の[[富田庄]]（[[阿波国]][[名東郡]]入田村（現徳島市[[入田町]]）一帯）に[[勧請]]された春日祠に起源を有つといい、[[蜂須賀家政]]の阿波入部に際して現在の大滝山東麓（眉山町大滝山1）に[[遷座]]されたと伝えるが（[[文化 (元号)|文化]]12年（1815年）の『[[阿波志]]』）、一説に[[天正]]14年（[[1586年]]）の家政による[[徳島城]]築城と共に、城下の[[鎮守]]として[[名東郡]]田宮村から迎えられ、同村から共に遷された勝福寺（通称春日寺）<ref>当神社境内にあったが、明治初年に廃されたという。</ref>を[[別当寺]]とするようになったともいう（[[昭和]]48年（1973年）の『徳島市史』）。[[慶長|慶長年間]]（16世紀末から17世紀初）に蜂須賀氏が[[徳島藩|徳島藩主]]となって以後、「春日大明神」と称して歴代藩主からの崇敬を受け、祭祀料として毎年供米10石が春日寺充てに寄進されたという。
[[明治]]6年（[[1873年]]）に現社名に改め、[[県社]]に列せられた。境内には[[眉山湧水群]]のひとつ春日水がある。周辺には[[三島神社 (徳島市)|三島神社]]、[[諏訪神社 (徳島市)|諏訪神社]]がある。
== 境内社 == * 豊玉比賣神社（祭神・天石門別豊玉比賣（[[トヨタマヒメ]]）、式内社） ** [[徳島城]]内にあった竜王神社が[[国瑞彦神社]]に合祀された後、さらに当神社に移され、合祀となった。 * 若宮神社（祭神・[[天忍雲根命]]） * 秋葉神社（祭神・[[天照大御神]]、[[大巳貴命]]、[[波邇夜須毘売神|埴安姫神]]、[[保食神]]、[[少彦名命]]）
== 交通 == * [[四国旅客鉄道|JR]][[徳島駅]]から車で約5分。
== 脚注 == {{脚注ヘルプ}} {{reflist}}
== 関連項目 == * 徳島市中五社 ** [[諏訪神社 (徳島市)|諏訪神社]] - 徳島市[[南佐古三番町]] ** [[四所神社 (徳島市)|四所神社]] - 徳島市[[福島 (徳島市)|福島]] ** [[八幡神社 (徳島市)|八幡神社]] - 徳島市[[伊賀町 (徳島市)|伊賀町]] ** [[金刀比羅神社 (徳島市)|金刀比羅神社]] - 徳島市[[勢見町]] {{shinto-stub}} {{神道 横}} {{DEFAULTSORT:かすかしんしや とくしまし}} [[Category:徳島県の旧県社]] [[Category:徳島市の神社]] [[Category:春日神社]] [[Category:眉山]]

[[File:Kasugasui.jpeg|thumb|250px|right|Kasuga Spring (春日水)]] '''Kasuga Shrine''' (春日神社) is a [[:en:Shinto shrine|Shinto shrine]] located in {{ill|Myozan, Tokushima City|ja|眉山町|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Myozan, Tokushima City|qq=|1=Bizanchō|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11582582}}, [[:en:Tokushima Prefecture|Tokushima Prefecture]], Japan. It is situated on the eastern foothills of [[:en:Mount Bizan|Mount Bizan]].
== Deities == The shrine enshrines the following four [[:en:Column|Kami]] (deities), identical to those of [[:en:Kasuga-taisha|Kasuga-taisha]] in [[:en:Nara Prefecture|Nara Prefecture]]: * {{ill|Takemikazuchi|ja|武甕槌命|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Takemikazuchi|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki [[Category:Kasuga Redirects]]s to タケミカヅチ}} * {{ill|Izanagi-no-Mikoto|ja|斎主命|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Izanagi-no-Mikoto|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki [[Category:Kasuga Redirects]]s to 経津主神|1=Futsunushi|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q1107286}} * {{ill|Amenokoyane no Mikoto|ja|天児屋根命|1=Ame-no-Koyane|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Amenokoyane no Mikoto|13=User:Immanuelle/Ame-no-Koyane|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki [[Category:Kasuga Redirects]]s to 天児屋命}} * [[:en:Himegami|Hime no Kami]]
== History == The shrine traces its origins to a {{ill|Kasuga-taisha|lt=Kasuga-taisha|lt=Kasuga Shrine|ja|春日祠|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kasuga Shrine|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}} enshrined at the Kasuga territory in {{ill|Tomi-da|ja|富田庄|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Tomi-da|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki [[Category:Kasuga Redirects]]s to 富田荘|1=Tomi-da|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q23996934}} (modern {{ill|Irida|ja|入田町|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Irida|qq=|1=Nyuta, Tokushima|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11389001}}, Tokushima City), a former estate of Kasuga Shrine in [[:en:Yamato Province|Yamato Province]]. It is said to have been relocated to its current site at Otakiyama during the transfer of power to the [[:en:Hachisuka clan|Hachisuka clan]] in 1586, coinciding with the construction of [[:en:Tokushima Castle|Tokushima Castle]]. Another account suggests the shrine was moved from {{ill|Tamiya Village|ja|田宮村|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Tamiya Village|qq=|1=Tamiya|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11576502}} along with Shofuku-ji Temple, which later became the shrine’s {{ill|Bettōji|ja|別当寺|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Bettōji|qq=|comment=changed title based on wikidata|1=bettō-ji|WD=Q11396755}} before its abolition in the early [[:en:Meiji era|Meiji period]].<ref>According to the ''Awa-shi'' (阿波志), compiled in 1815.</ref>
During the [[:en:Keichō|Keicho era]] (late 16th to early 17th century), the shrine was referred to as "Kasuga Daimyōjin" and received significant patronage from the Hachisuka clan, including an annual offering of 10 koku of rice. In 1873, it was officially renamed Kasuga Shrine and designated as a {{ill|Ken-sha|ja|県社|1=Prefectural Shrine|qid=Q90139226}}{{efn|Ken-sha|lt=Ken-sha|1=modern system of ranked Shinto shrines|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ken-sha|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki [[Category:Kasuga Redirects]]s to 近代社格制度|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q712534}}. The shrine also features "Kasuga Spring" (春日水), one of the notable {{ill|Mount Bizan springs|ja|眉山湧水群|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Mount Bizan springs|qq=|1=Bizan Springs|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11582583}}.
== Sub-Shrines == The shrine complex includes the following sub-shrines: * '''Toyotama-hime Shrine''' (deity: {{ill|Toyotama-hime|ja|豊玉比賣|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Toyotama-hime|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}}) ** Enshrines the deity formerly worshipped at Ryuo Shrine within Tokushima Castle. * '''Wakamiya Shrine''' (deity: {{ill|Ame-no-Kumunushi|ja|天忍雲根命|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ame-no-Kumunushi|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki [[Category:Kasuga Redirects]]s to 天押雲根命|1=Ame-no-Oshikumone|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q91088537}}) * '''Akiba Shrine''' (deity: {{ill|Amaterasu|ja|天照大御神|1=Amaterasu|lt=Amaterasu Ōmikami|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Amaterasu|13=User:Immanuelle/Amaterasu|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki [[Category:Kasuga Redirects]]s to 天照大神}}, {{ill|Onamuchi|ja|大巳貴命|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Onamuchi|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki [[Category:Kasuga Redirects]]s to 大国主|1=Ōkuninushi|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q276944}}, {{ill|Haniyasubime|ja|埴安姫神|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Haniyasubime|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}}, [[:en:Ukemochi|Ukemochi]], {{ill|Sukunabikona|ja|少彦名命|1=Sukunabikona|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Sukunabikona|13=User:Immanuelle/Sukunabikona|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki [[Category:Kasuga Redirects]]s to スクナビコナ}})
== Transportation == * '''By car''': 5 minutes from [[:en:Tokushima Station|Tokushima Station]], [[:en:Shikoku Railway Company|Shikoku Railway Company]] (JR Shikoku).

'''Kasuga Shrine''' (春日神社) is a Shinto shrine located in {{ill|Bizan Town|ja|眉山町|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Bizan Town|qq=|1=Bizanchō|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11582582}}, [[:en:Tokushima (city)|Tokushima City]], [[:en:Tokushima Prefecture|Tokushima Prefecture]], Japan. It is situated at the eastern foot of Mount Ōtakiyama within Bizan.
== Enshrined Deities == The shrine venerates the {{ill|Kasuga-no-Kami|fr|Kasuga_no_Kami|ja|春日神|1=Kasuga-no-Kami|2=ja|3=春日神|4=fr|5=Kasuga no == History == The shrine traces its origins to a Kasuga Shrine originally enshrined in {{ill|Tomida Manor|ja|富田庄|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Tomida Manor|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki [[Category:Kasuga Redirects]]s to 富田荘|1=Tomida Manor|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q23996934}} of [[:en:Yamato Province|Yamato Province]] (present-day {{ill|Iritamura|ja|入田村|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Iritamura|qq=|1=Iritamura|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11388998}} in [[:en:Tokushima City|Tokushima City]]). During the invasion of [[Awa Province]] by [[:en:Hachisuka Iemasa|Hachisuka Iemasa]], the shrine was relocated to its current location at Ōtakiyama 1 in {{ill|Bizan Town|ja|眉山町|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Bizan Town|qq=|1=Bizanchō|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11582582}}. This history is documented in the *Awa-shi* from 1815 (Bunka 12). Another theory suggests that in 1586 (Tenshō 14), during the construction of [https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tokushima_Castle Tokushima Castle], the shrine was moved from {{ill|Tamiyamura|ja|田宮村|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Tamiyamura|qq=|1=Tamiya|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11576502}} to serve as the castle's tutelary shrine.
Under the governance of the [[:en:Hachisuka clan|Hachisuka clan]], the shrine, known as "Kasuga Daimyōjin," gained significant reverence, receiving annual offerings of 10 koku of rice. In 1873 (Meiji 6), the shrine's name was officially changed to Kasuga Shrine, and it was designated a Prefectural Shrine. The site includes the spring known as *Kasuga Water*, part of the {{ill|Bizan Springs|ja|眉山湧水群|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Bizan Springs|qq=|1=Bizan Springs|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11582583}}.
== Subsidiary Shrines == * '''Toyotama-Hime Shrine''' (deity: [[:en:Toyotama-hime|Toyotama-Hime-no-Mikoto]], designated as an ancient shrine) ''' The shrine was originally located within [https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tokushima_Castle Tokushima Castle] as Ryūō Shrine, later merged into Kunikazu Shrine before being relocated here. * '''Wakamiya Shrine''' (deity: {{ill|Ame-no-Oshikumone|ja|天押雲根命|en|draft:Ame-no-Oshikumone|simple|User:Immanuelle/Ame-no-Oshikumone|fr|Utilisateur:Immanuelle/Ame-no-Oshikumone|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ame-no-Oshikumone|qq=}}) * '''Akiba Shrine''' (deity: [[Amaterasu]], [[Ōkuninushi|Ōkuninushi-no-Mikoto]], [[Haniyasu-hiko and Haniyasu-hime|Haniyasu-hime-no-Mikoto]], [[:en:Ukemochi|Ukemochi-no-Kami]], [[Sukunabikona|Sukunahikona-no-Kami]])
== Transportation == * Approximately 5 minutes by car from [[JR Tokushima Station]].
== Related Articles == * Tokushima City Central Five Shrines: ''' {{ill|Suwa Shrine (Tokushima City)|ja|諏訪神社 (徳島市)|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Suwa Shrine (Tokushima City)|qq=}} - Located in Minamisako, Tokushima City ''' {{ill|Shisho Shrine (Tokushima)|ja|四所神社 (徳島市)|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Shisho Shrine (Tokushima City)|qq=}} - Located in Fukushima, Tokushima City ''' {{ill|Hachiman Shrine (Tokushima City)|ja|八幡神社 (徳島市)|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Hachiman Shrine (Tokushima City)|qq=}} - Located in Iga Town, Tokushima City ''' {{ill|Konpira Shrine (Tokushima)|ja|金刀比羅神社 (徳島市)|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kotohira Shrine (Tokushima City)|qq=}} - Located in Semimachi, Tokushima City

[[File:Kasugasui.jpeg|thumb|250px|right|Kasuga Spring (春日水)]] '''Kasuga Shrine''' (春日神社) is a [[:en:Shinto shrine|Shinto shrine]] located in {{ill|Myozan, Tokushima City|ja|眉山町|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Myozan, Tokushima City|qq=|1=Bizanchō|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11582582}}, [[:en:Tokushima Prefecture|Tokushima Prefecture]], Japan. It is situated on the eastern foothills of [[:en:Mount Bizan|Mount Bizan]].
== Deities == The shrine enshrines the following four [[:en:Column|Kami]] (deities), identical to those of [[:en:Kasuga-taisha|Kasuga-taisha]] in [[:en:Nara Prefecture|Nara Prefecture]]: * {{ill|Takemikazuchi|ja|武甕槌命|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Takemikazuchi|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki [[Category:Kasuga Redirects]]s to タケミカヅチ}} * {{ill|Izanagi-no-Mikoto|ja|斎主命|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Izanagi-no-Mikoto|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki [[Category:Kasuga Redirects]]s to 経津主神|1=Futsunushi|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q1107286}} * {{ill|Amenokoyane no Mikoto|ja|天児屋根命|1=Ame-no-Koyane|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Amenokoyane no Mikoto|13=User:Immanuelle/Ame-no-Koyane|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki [[Category:Kasuga Redirects]]s to 天児屋命}} * [[:en:Himegami|Hime no Kami]]
== History == The shrine traces its origins to a {{ill|Kasuga-taisha|lt=Kasuga-taisha|lt=Kasuga Shrine|ja|春日祠|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kasuga Shrine|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}} enshrined at the Kasuga territory in {{ill|Tomi-da|ja|富田庄|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Tomi-da|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki [[Category:Kasuga Redirects]]s to 富田荘|1=Tomi-da|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q23996934}} (modern {{ill|Irida|ja|入田町|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Irida|qq=|1=Nyuta, Tokushima|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11389001}}, Tokushima City), a former estate of Kasuga Shrine in [[:en:Yamato Province|Yamato Province]]. It is said to have been relocated to its current site at Otakiyama during the transfer of power to the [[:en:Hachisuka clan|Hachisuka clan]] in 1586, coinciding with the construction of [[:en:Tokushima Castle|Tokushima Castle]]. Another account suggests the shrine was moved from {{ill|Tamiya Village|ja|田宮村|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Tamiya Village|qq=|1=Tamiya|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11576502}} along with Shofuku-ji Temple, which later became the shrine’s {{ill|Bettōji|ja|別当寺|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Bettōji|qq=|comment=changed title based on wikidata|1=bettō-ji|WD=Q11396755}} before its abolition in the early [[:en:Meiji era|Meiji period]].<ref>According to the ''Awa-shi'' (阿波志), compiled in 1815.</ref>
During the [[:en:Keichō|Keicho era]] (late 16th to early 17th century), the shrine was referred to as "Kasuga Daimyōjin" and received significant patronage from the Hachisuka clan, including an annual offering of 10 koku of rice. In 1873, it was officially renamed Kasuga Shrine and designated as a {{ill|Ken-sha|ja|県社|1=Prefectural Shrine|WD=Q90139226}}{{efn|Ken-sha|lt=Ken-sha|1=modern system of ranked Shinto shrines|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ken-sha|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki [[Category:Kasuga Redirects]]s to 近代社格制度|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q712534}}. The shrine also features "Kasuga Spring" (春日水), one of the notable {{ill|Mount Bizan springs|ja|眉山湧水群|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Mount Bizan springs|qq=|1=Bizan Springs|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11582583}}.
== Sub-Shrines == The shrine complex includes the following sub-shrines: * '''Toyotama-hime Shrine''' (deity: {{ill|Toyotama-hime|ja|豊玉比賣|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Toyotama-hime|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}}) ** Enshrines the deity formerly worshipped at Ryuo Shrine within Tokushima Castle. * '''Wakamiya Shrine''' (deity: {{ill|Ame-no-Kumunushi|ja|天忍雲根命|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ame-no-Kumunushi|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki [[Category:Kasuga Redirects]]s to 天押雲根命|1=Ame-no-Oshikumone|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q91088537}}) * '''Akiba Shrine''' (deity: {{ill|Amaterasu|ja|天照大御神|1=Amaterasu|lt=Amaterasu Ōmikami|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Amaterasu|13=User:Immanuelle/Amaterasu|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki [[Category:Kasuga Redirects]]s to 天照大神}}, {{ill|Onamuchi|ja|大巳貴命|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Onamuchi|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki [[Category:Kasuga Redirects]]s to 大国主|1=Ōkuninushi|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q276944}}, {{ill|Haniyasubime|ja|埴安姫神|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Haniyasubime|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}}, [[:en:Ukemochi|Ukemochi]], {{ill|Sukunabikona|ja|少彦名命|1=Sukunabikona|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Sukunabikona|13=User:Immanuelle/Sukunabikona|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki [[Category:Kasuga Redirects]]s to スクナビコナ}})

== History == The shrine traces its origins to a Kasuga Shrine originally enshrined in {{ill|Tomida Manor|ja|富田庄|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Tomida Manor|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki [[Category:Kasuga Redirects]]s to 富田荘|1=Tomida Manor|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q23996934}} of [[:en:Yamato Province|Yamato Province]] (present-day {{ill|Iritamura|ja|入田村|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Iritamura|qq=|1=Iritamura|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11388998}} in [[:en:Tokushima City|Tokushima City]]). During the invasion of [[Awa Province]] by [[:en:Hachisuka Iemasa|Hachisuka Iemasa]], the shrine was relocated to its current location at Ōtakiyama 1 in {{ill|Bizan Town|ja|眉山町|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Bizan Town|qq=|1=Bizanchō|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11582582}}. This history is documented in the *Awa-shi* from 1815 (Bunka 12). Another theory suggests that in 1586 (Tenshō 14), during the construction of [https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tokushima_Castle Tokushima Castle], the shrine was moved from {{ill|Tamiyamura|ja|田宮村|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Tamiyamura|qq=|1=Tamiya|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11576502}} to serve as the castle's tutelary shrine.
Under the governance of the [[:en:Hachisuka clan|Hachisuka clan]], the shrine, known as "Kasuga Daimyōjin," gained significant reverence, receiving annual offerings of 10 koku of rice. In 1873 (Meiji 6), the shrine's name was officially changed to Kasuga Shrine, and it was designated a Prefectural Shrine. The site includes the spring known as *Kasuga Water*, part of the {{ill|Bizan Springs|ja|眉山湧水群|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Bizan Springs|qq=|1=Bizan Springs|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11582583}}.
== Subsidiary Shrines == * '''Toyotama-Hime Shrine''' (deity: [[:en:Toyotama-hime|Toyotama-Hime-no-Mikoto]], designated as an ancient shrine) ''' The shrine was originally located within [https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tokushima_Castle Tokushima Castle] as Ryūō Shrine, later merged into Kunikazu Shrine before being relocated here. * '''Wakamiya Shrine''' (deity: {{ill|Ame-no-Oshikumone|ja|天押雲根命|en|draft:Ame-no-Oshikumone|simple|User:Immanuelle/Ame-no-Oshikumone|fr|Utilisateur:Immanuelle/Ame-no-Oshikumone|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ame-no-Oshikumone|qq=}}) * '''Akiba Shrine''' (deity: [[Amaterasu]], [[Ōkuninushi|Ōkuninushi-no-Mikoto]], [[Haniyasu-hiko and Haniyasu-hime|Haniyasu-hime-no-Mikoto]], [[:en:Ukemochi|Ukemochi-no-Kami]], [[Sukunabikona|Sukunahikona-no-Kami]])
== Transportation == * Approximately 5 minutes by car from [[JR Tokushima Station]].

to 近代社格制度|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q712534}} | founded = 1586 (Tenshō 14) | main_building = [[:en:Kasuga-zukuri|Kasuga-zukuri]] | festivals = [[:en:April 17|April 17]], [[:en:October [[File:Kasugasui.jpeg|thumb|250px|right|Kasuga Spring (春日水)]] '''Kasuga Shrine''' (春日神社) is a [[:en:Shinto shrine|Shinto shrine]] located in {{ill|Myozan, Tokushima City|ja|眉山町|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Myozan, Tokushima City|1=Bizanchō|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11582582}}, [[:en:Tokushima Prefecture|Tokushima Prefecture]], Japan. It is situated on the eastern foothills of [[:en:Mount Bizan|Mount Bizan]].
== Deities == The shrine enshrines the following four [[:en:Column|Kami]] (deities), identical to those of [[:en:Kasuga-taisha|Kasuga-taisha]] in [[:en:Nara Prefecture|Nara Prefecture]]: * {{ill|Takemikazuchi|ja|武甕槌命|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Takemikazuchi|ja_comment=jawiki [[Category:Kasuga Redirects]]s to タケミカヅチ}} * {{ill|Izanagi-no-Mikoto|ja|斎主命|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Izanagi-no-Mikoto|ja_comment=jawiki [[Category:Kasuga Redirects]]s to 経津主神|1=Futsunushi|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q1107286}} * {{ill|Amenokoyane no Mikoto|ja|天児屋根命|1=Ame-no-Koyane|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Amenokoyane no Mikoto|13=User:Immanuelle/Ame-no-Koyane|ja_comment=jawiki [[Category:Kasuga Redirects]]s to 天児屋命}} * [[:en:Himegami|Hime no Kami]]
== History == The shrine traces its origins to a {{ill|Kasuga-taisha|lt=Kasuga-taisha|lt=Kasuga Shrine|ja|春日祠|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kasuga Shrine|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}} enshrined at the Kasuga territory in {{ill|Tomi-da|ja|富田庄|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Tomi-da|ja_comment=jawiki [[Category:Kasuga Redirects]]s to 富田荘|1=Tomi-da|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q23996934}} (modern {{ill|Irida|ja|入田町|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Irida|1=Nyuta, Tokushima|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11389001}}, Tokushima City), a former estate of Kasuga Shrine in [[:en:Yamato Province|Yamato Province]]. It is said to have been relocated to its current site at Otakiyama during the transfer of power to the [[:en:Hachisuka clan|Hachisuka clan]] in 1586, coinciding with the construction of [[:en:Tokushima Castle|Tokushima Castle]]. Another account suggests the shrine was moved from {{ill|Tamiya Village|ja|田宮村|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Tamiya Village|1=Tamiya|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11576502}} along with Shofuku-ji Temple, which later became the shrine’s {{ill|Bettōji|ja|別当寺|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Bettōji|comment=changed title based on wikidata|1=bettō-ji|WD=Q11396755}} before its abolition in the early [[:en:Meiji era|Meiji period]].<ref>According to the ''Awa-shi'' (阿波志), compiled in 1815.</ref>
During the [[:en:Keichō|Keicho era]] (late 16th to early 17th century), the shrine was referred to as "Kasuga Daimyōjin" and received significant patronage from the Hachisuka clan, including an annual offering of 10 koku of rice. In 1873, it was officially renamed Kasuga Shrine and designated as a {{ill|Ken-sha|ja|県社|1=Prefectural Shrine|WD=Q90139226}}{{efn|Ken-sha|lt=Ken-sha|1=modern system of ranked Shinto shrines|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ken-sha|ja_comment=jawiki [[Category:Kasuga Redirects]]s to 近代社格制度|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q712534}}. The shrine also features "Kasuga Spring" (春日水), one of the notable {{ill|Mount Bizan springs|ja|眉山湧水群|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Mount Bizan springs|1=Bizan Springs|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11582583}}.
== Sub-Shrines == The shrine complex includes the following sub-shrines: * '''Toyotama-hime Shrine''' (deity: {{ill|Toyotama-hime|ja|豊玉比賣|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Toyotama-hime|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}}) ** Enshrines the deity formerly worshipped at Ryuo Shrine within Tokushima Castle. * '''Wakamiya Shrine''' (deity: {{ill|Ame-no-Kumunushi|ja|天忍雲根命|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ame-no-Kumunushi|ja_comment=jawiki [[Category:Kasuga Redirects]]s to 天押雲根命|1=Ame-no-Oshikumone|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q91088537}}) * '''Akiba Shrine''' (deity: {{ill|Amaterasu|ja|天照大御神|1=Amaterasu|lt=Amaterasu Ōmikami|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Amaterasu|13=User:Immanuelle/Amaterasu|ja_comment=jawiki [[Category:Kasuga Redirects]]s to 天照大神}}, {{ill|Onamuchi|ja|大巳貴命|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Onamuchi|ja_comment=jawiki [[Category:Kasuga Redirects]]s to 大国主|1=Ōkuninushi|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q276944}}, {{ill|Haniyasubime|ja|埴安姫神|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Haniyasubime|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}}, [[:en:Ukemochi|Ukemochi]], {{ill|Sukunabikona|ja|少彦名命|1=Sukunabikona|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Sukunabikona|13=User:Immanuelle/Sukunabikona|ja_comment=jawiki [[Category:Kasuga Redirects]]s to スクナビコナ}})

== History == The shrine traces its origins to a Kasuga Shrine originally enshrined in {{ill|Tomida Manor|ja|富田庄|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Tomida Manor|ja_comment=jawiki [[Category:Kasuga Redirects]]s to 富田荘|1=Tomida Manor|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q23996934}} of [[:en:Yamato Province|Yamato Province]] (present-day {{ill|Iritamura|ja|入田村|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Iritamura|1=Iritamura|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11388998}} in [[:en:Tokushima City|Tokushima City]]). During the invasion of [[Awa Province]] by [[:en:Hachisuka Iemasa|Hachisuka Iemasa]], the shrine was relocated to its current location at Ōtakiyama 1 in {{ill|Bizan Town|ja|眉山町|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Bizan Town|1=Bizanchō|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11582582}}. This history is documented in the *Awa-shi* from 1815 (Bunka 12). Another theory suggests that in 1586 (Tenshō 14), during the construction of [https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tokushima_Castle Tokushima Castle], the shrine was moved from {{ill|Tamiyamura|ja|田宮村|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Tamiyamura|1=Tamiya|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11576502}} to serve as the castle's tutelary shrine.
Under the governance of the [[:en:Hachisuka clan|Hachisuka clan]], the shrine, known as "Kasuga Daimyōjin," gained significant reverence, receiving annual offerings of 10 koku of rice. In 1873 (Meiji 6), the shrine's name was officially changed to Kasuga Shrine, and it was designated a Prefectural Shrine. The site includes the spring known as *Kasuga Water*, part of the {{ill|Bizan Springs|ja|眉山湧水群|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Bizan Springs|1=Bizan Springs|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11582583}}.
== Subsidiary Shrines == * '''Toyotama-Hime Shrine''' (deity: [[:en:Toyotama-hime|Toyotama-Hime-no-Mikoto]], designated as an ancient shrine) ''' The shrine was originally located within [https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tokushima_Castle Tokushima Castle] as Ryūō Shrine, later merged into Kunikazu Shrine before being relocated here. * '''Wakamiya Shrine''' (deity: {{ill|Ame-no-Oshikumone|ja|天押雲根命|en|draft:Ame-no-Oshikumone|simple|User:Immanuelle/Ame-no-Oshikumone|fr|Utilisateur:Immanuelle/Ame-no-Oshikumone|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ame-no-Oshikumone|qq=}}) * '''Akiba Shrine''' (deity: [[Amaterasu]], [[Ōkuninushi|Ōkuninushi-no-Mikoto]], [[Haniyasu-hiko and Haniyasu-hime|Haniyasu-hime-no-Mikoto]], [[:en:Ukemochi|Ukemochi-no-Kami]], [[Sukunabikona|Sukunahikona-no-Kami]])
