== Deities == The shrine enshrines the following four {{ill|Column|en|Column|WD=Q4817|lt=Kami}} (deities), identical to those of {{ill|Kasuga-taisha|en|Kasuga-taisha|WD=Q714559|lt=Kasuga-taisha}} in {{ill|Nara Prefecture|en|Nara Prefecture|WD=Q131287|lt=Nara Prefecture}}: * {{ill|Takemikazuchi|ja|武甕槌命|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Takemikazuchi|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to タケミカヅチ}} * {{ill|Izanagi-no-Mikoto|ja|斎主命|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Izanagi-no-Mikoto|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 経津主神}} * {{ill|Amenokoyane no Mikoto|ja|天児屋根命|1=Ame-no-Koyane|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Amenokoyane no Mikoto|13=User:Immanuelle/Ame-no-Koyane|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 天児屋命}} * {{ill|Himegami|en|Himegami|WD=Q22070227|lt=Hime no Kami}}
== History == The shrine traces its origins to a {{ill|Kasuga-taisha|lt=Kasuga-taisha|lt=Kasuga Shrine|ja|春日祠|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kasuga Shrine|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}} enshrined at the Kasuga territory in {{ill|Tomi-da|ja|富田庄|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Tomi-da|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 富田荘}} (modern {{ill|Irida|ja|入田町|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Irida|qq=}}, Tokushima City), a former estate of Kasuga Shrine in {{ill|Yamato Province|en|Yamato Province|WD=Q907495|lt=Yamato Province}}. It is said to have been relocated to its current site at Otakiyama during the transfer of power to the {{ill|Hachisuka clan|en|Hachisuka clan|WD=Q2975261|lt=Hachisuka clan}} in 1586, coinciding with the construction of {{ill|Tokushima Castle|en|Tokushima Castle|WD=Q8011246|lt=Tokushima Castle}}. Another account suggests the shrine was moved from {{ill|Tamiya Village|ja|田宮村|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Tamiya Village|qq=}} along with Shofuku-ji Temple, which later became the shrine’s {{ill|Bettōji|ja|別当寺|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Bettōji|qq=|comment=enwiki is a redirect}} before its abolition in the early {{ill|Meiji era|en|Meiji era|WD=Q3125096|lt=Meiji period}}.<ref>According to the ''Awa-shi'' (阿波志), compiled in 1815.</ref>
During the {{ill|Keichō|en|Keichō|WD=Q1328185|lt=Keicho era}} (late 16th to early 17th century), the shrine was referred to as "Kasuga Daimyōjin" and received significant patronage from the Hachisuka clan, including an annual offering of 10 koku of rice. In 1873, it was officially renamed Kasuga Shrine and designated as a {{ill|Ken-sha|ja|県社|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ken-sha|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 近代社格制度}}. The shrine also features "Kasuga Spring" (春日水), one of the notable {{ill|Mount Bizan springs|ja|眉山湧水群|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Mount Bizan springs|qq=}}.

|}
== History == The shrine traces its origins to a Kasuga Shrine originally enshrined in {{ill|Tomida Manor|ja|富田庄|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Tomida Manor|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 富田荘}} of [[Yamato Province]] (present-day {{ill|Iritamura|ja|入田村|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Iritamura|qq=}} in [[Tokushima City|Tokushima City]]). During the invasion of [[Awa Province]] by [[Hachisuka Iemasa]], the shrine was relocated to its current location at Ōtakiyama 1 in {{ill|Bizan Town|ja|眉山町|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Bizan Town|qq=}}. This history is documented in the *Awa-shi* from 1815 (Bunka 12). Another theory suggests that in 1586 (Tenshō 14), during the construction of [https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tokushima_Castle Tokushima Castle], the shrine was moved from {{ill|Tamiyamura|ja|田宮村|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Tamiyamura|qq=}} to serve as the castle's tutelary shrine.
Under the governance of the [[Hachisuka clan]], the shrine, known as "Kasuga Daimyōjin," gained significant reverence, receiving annual offerings of 10 koku of rice. In 1873 (Meiji 6), the shrine's name was officially changed to Kasuga Shrine, and it was designated a Prefectural Shrine. The site includes the spring known as *Kasuga Water*, part of the {{ill|Bizan Springs|ja|眉山湧水群|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Bizan Springs|qq=}}.
== Subsidiary Shrines == * '''Toyotama-Hime Shrine''' (deity: [[Toyotama-hime|Toyotama-Hime-no-Mikoto]], designated as an ancient shrine) ''' The shrine was originally located within [https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tokushima_Castle Tokushima Castle] as Ryūō Shrine, later merged into Kunikazu Shrine before being relocated here. * '''Wakamiya Shrine''' (deity: {{ill|Ame-no-Oshikumone|ja|天押雲根命|en|draft:Ame-no-Oshikumone|simple|User:Immanuelle/Ame-no-Oshikumone|fr|Utilisateur:Immanuelle/Ame-no-Oshikumone|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ame-no-Oshikumone|qq=}}) * '''Akiba Shrine''' (deity: [[Amaterasu]], [[Ōkuninushi|Ōkuninushi-no-Mikoto]], [[Haniyasu-hiko and Haniyasu-hime|Haniyasu-hime-no-Mikoto]], [[Ukemochi|Ukemochi-no-Kami]], [[Sukunabikona|Sukunahikona-no-Kami]])
== Transportation == * Approximately 5 minutes by car from [[JR Tokushima Station]].
== Related Articles == * Tokushima City Central Five Shrines: ''' {{ill|Suwa Shrine (Tokushima City)|ja|諏訪神社 (徳島市)|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Suwa Shrine (Tokushima City)|qq=}} - Located in Minamisako, Tokushima City ''' {{ill|Shisho Shrine (Tokushima)|ja|四所神社 (徳島市)|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Shisho Shrine (Tokushima City)|qq=}} - Located in Fukushima, Tokushima City ''' {{ill|Hachiman Shrine (Tokushima City)|ja|八幡神社 (徳島市)|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Hachiman Shrine (Tokushima City)|qq=}} - Located in Iga Town, Tokushima City ''' {{ill|Konpira Shrine (Tokushima)|ja|金刀比羅神社 (徳島市)|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kotohira Shrine (Tokushima City)|qq=}} - Located in Semimachi, Tokushima City

[[File:Kasugasui.jpeg|thumb|250px|right|Kasuga Spring (春日水)]] '''Kasuga Shrine''' (春日神社) is a {{ill|Shinto shrine|en|Shinto shrine|WD=Q845945|lt=Shinto shrine|1=Shinto shrine}} located in {{ill|Myozan, Tokushima City|ja|眉山町|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Myozan, Tokushima City|qq=}}, {{ill|Tokushima Prefecture|en|Tokushima Prefecture|WD=Q160734|lt=Tokushima Prefecture|1=Tokushima Prefecture}}, Japan. It is situated on the eastern foothills of {{ill|Mount Bizan|ja|眉山|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Mount Bizan|qq=}}.
== Deities == The shrine enshrines the following four {{ill|Column|en|Column|WD=Q4817|lt=Kami|1=Column}} (deities), identical to those of {{ill|Kasuga-taisha|en|Kasuga-taisha|WD=Q714559|lt=Kasuga-taisha|1=Kasuga-taisha}} in {{ill|Nara Prefecture|en|Nara Prefecture|WD=Q131287|lt=Nara Prefecture|1=Nara Prefecture}}: * {{ill|Takemikazuchi|ja|武甕槌命|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Takemikazuchi|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to タケミカヅチ}} * {{ill|Izanagi-no-Mikoto|ja|斎主命|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Izanagi-no-Mikoto|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 経津主神}} * {{ill|Amenokoyane no Mikoto|ja|天児屋根命|1=Ame-no-Koyane|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Amenokoyane no Mikoto|13=User:Immanuelle/Ame-no-Koyane|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 天児屋命}} * {{ill|Himegami|en|Himegami|WD=Q22070227|lt=Hime no Kami|1=Himegami}}
== History == The shrine traces its origins to a {{ill|Kasuga-taisha|lt=Kasuga-taisha|lt=Kasuga Shrine|ja|春日祠|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kasuga Shrine|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}} enshrined at the Kasuga territory in {{ill|Tomi-da|ja|富田庄|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Tomi-da|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 富田荘}} (modern {{ill|Irida|ja|入田町|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Irida|qq=}}, Tokushima City), a former estate of Kasuga Shrine in {{ill|Yamato Province|en|Yamato Province|WD=Q907495|lt=Yamato Province|1=Yamato Province}}. It is said to have been relocated to its current site at Otakiyama during the transfer of power to the {{ill|Hachisuka clan|en|Hachisuka clan|WD=Q2975261|lt=Hachisuka clan|1=Hachisuka clan}} in 1586, coinciding with the construction of {{ill|Tokushima Castle|en|Tokushima Castle|WD=Q8011246|lt=Tokushima Castle|1=Tokushima Castle}}. Another account suggests the shrine was moved from {{ill|Tamiya Village|ja|田宮村|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Tamiya Village|qq=}} along with Shofuku-ji Temple, which later became the shrine’s {{ill|Bettōji|ja|別当寺|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Bettōji|qq=|comment=enwiki is a redirect}} before its abolition in the early {{ill|Meiji era|en|Meiji era|WD=Q3125096|lt=Meiji period|1=Meiji era}}.<ref>According to the ''Awa-shi'' (阿波志), compiled in 1815.</ref>
During the {{ill|Keichō|en|Keichō|WD=Q1328185|lt=Keicho era|1=Keichō}} (late 16th to early 17th century), the shrine was referred to as "Kasuga Daimyōjin" and received significant patronage from the Hachisuka clan, including an annual offering of 10 koku of rice. In 1873, it was officially renamed Kasuga Shrine and designated as a {{ill|Ken-sha|ja|県社|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ken-sha|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 近代社格制度}}. The shrine also features "Kasuga Spring" (春日水), one of the notable {{ill|Mount Bizan springs|ja|眉山湧水群|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Mount Bizan springs|qq=}}.
== Sub-Shrines == The shrine complex includes the following sub-shrines: * '''Toyotama-hime Shrine''' (deity: {{ill|Toyotama-hime|ja|豊玉比賣|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Toyotama-hime|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}}) ** Enshrines the deity formerly worshipped at Ryuo Shrine within Tokushima Castle. * '''Wakamiya Shrine''' (deity: {{ill|Ame-no-Kumunushi|ja|天忍雲根命|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ame-no-Kumunushi|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 天押雲根命}}) * '''Akiba Shrine''' (deity: {{ill|Amaterasu|ja|天照大御神|1=Amaterasu|lt=Amaterasu Ōmikami|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Amaterasu|13=User:Immanuelle/Amaterasu|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 天照大神}}, {{ill|Onamuchi|ja|大巳貴命|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Onamuchi|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 大国主}}, {{ill|Haniyasubime|ja|埴安姫神|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Haniyasubime|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}}, {{ill|Ukemochi|en|Ukemochi|WD=Q2280323|lt=Ukemochi|1=Ukemochi}}, {{ill|Sukunabikona|ja|少彦名命|1=Sukunabikona|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Sukunabikona|13=User:Immanuelle/Sukunabikona|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to スクナビコナ}})
== Transportation == * '''By car''': 5 minutes from {{ill|Tokushima Station|en|Tokushima Station|WD=Q860775|lt=Tokushima Station|1=Tokushima Station}}, {{ill|Shikoku Railway Company|en|Shikoku Railway Company|WD=Q496531|lt=Shikoku Railway Company|1=Shikoku Railway Company}} (JR Shikoku).

== History == The shrine traces its origins to a Kasuga Shrine originally enshrined in {{ill|Tomida Manor|ja|富田庄|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Tomida Manor|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 富田荘}} of [[Yamato Province]] (present-day {{ill|Iritamura|ja|入田村|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Iritamura|qq=}} in [[Tokushima City|Tokushima City]]). During the invasion of [[Awa Province]] by [[Hachisuka Iemasa]], the shrine was relocated to its current location at Ōtakiyama 1 in {{ill|Bizan Town|ja|眉山町|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Bizan Town|qq=}}. This history is documented in the *Awa-shi* from 1815 (Bunka 12). Another theory suggests that in 1586 (Tenshō 14), during the construction of [https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tokushima_Castle Tokushima Castle], the shrine was moved from {{ill|Tamiyamura|ja|田宮村|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Tamiyamura|qq=}} to serve as the castle's tutelary shrine.
Under the governance of the [[Hachisuka clan]], the shrine, known as "Kasuga Daimyōjin," gained significant reverence, receiving annual offerings of 10 koku of rice. In 1873 (Meiji 6), the shrine's name was officially changed to Kasuga Shrine, and it was designated a Prefectural Shrine. The site includes the spring known as *Kasuga Water*, part of the {{ill|Bizan Springs|ja|眉山湧水群|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Bizan Springs|qq=}}.

== History == The shrine traces its origins to a {{ill|Kasuga-taisha|lt=Kasuga-taisha|lt=Kasuga Shrine|ja|春日祠|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kasuga Shrine|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}} enshrined at the Kasuga territory in {{ill|Tomi-da|ja|富田庄|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Tomi-da|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 富田荘}} (modern {{ill|Irida|ja|入田町|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Irida|qq=}}, Tokushima City), a former estate of Kasuga Shrine in {{ill|Yamato Province|en|Yamato Province|WD=Q907495|lt=Yamato Province|1=Yamato Province}}. During the {{ill|Keichō|en|Keichō|WD=Q1328185|lt=Keicho era|1=Keichō}} (late 16th to early 17th century), the shrine was referred to as "Kasuga Daimyōjin" and received significant patronage from the Hachisuka clan, including an annual offering of 10 koku of rice. [[File:Kasugasui.jpeg|thumb|250px|right|Kasuga Spring (春日水)]] '''Kasuga Shrine''' (春日神社) is a {{ill|Shinto shrine|en|Shinto shrine|WD=Q845945|lt=Shinto shrine|1=Shinto shrine}} located in {{ill|Myozan, Tokushima City|ja|眉山町|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Myozan, Tokushima City|qq=}}, {{ill|Tokushima Prefecture|en|Tokushima Prefecture|WD=Q160734|lt=Tokushima Prefecture|1=Tokushima Prefecture}}, Japan. It is situated on the eastern foothills of {{ill|Mount Bizan|ja|眉山|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Mount Bizan|qq=}}.
== Deities == The shrine enshrines the following four {{ill|Column|en|Column|WD=Q4817|lt=Kami|1=Column}} (deities), identical to those of {{ill|Kasuga-taisha|en|Kasuga-taisha|WD=Q714559|lt=Kasuga-taisha|1=Kasuga-taisha}} in {{ill|Nara Prefecture|en|Nara Prefecture|WD=Q131287|lt=Nara Prefecture|1=Nara Prefecture}}: * {{ill|Takemikazuchi|ja|武甕槌命|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Takemikazuchi|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to タケミカヅチ}} * {{ill|Izanagi-no-Mikoto|ja|斎主命|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Izanagi-no-Mikoto|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 経津主神}} * {{ill|Amenokoyane no Mikoto|ja|天児屋根命|1=Ame-no-Koyane|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Amenokoyane no Mikoto|13=User:Immanuelle/Ame-no-Koyane|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 天児屋命}} * {{ill|Himegami|en|Himegami|WD=Q22070227|lt=Hime no Kami|1=Himegami}}
== History == The shrine traces its origins to a {{ill|Kasuga-taisha|lt=Kasuga-taisha|lt=Kasuga Shrine|ja|春日祠|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kasuga Shrine|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}} enshrined at the Kasuga territory in {{ill|Tomi-da|ja|富田庄|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Tomi-da|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 富田荘}} (modern {{ill|Irida|ja|入田町|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Irida|qq=}}, Tokushima City), a former estate of Kasuga Shrine in {{ill|Yamato Province|en|Yamato Province|WD=Q907495|lt=Yamato Province|1=Yamato Province}}. It is said to have been relocated to its current site at Otakiyama during the transfer of power to the {{ill|Hachisuka clan|en|Hachisuka clan|WD=Q2975261|lt=Hachisuka clan|1=Hachisuka clan}} in 1586, coinciding with the construction of {{ill|Tokushima Castle|en|Tokushima Castle|WD=Q8011246|lt=Tokushima Castle|1=Tokushima Castle}}. Another account suggests the shrine was moved from {{ill|Tamiya Village|ja|田宮村|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Tamiya Village|qq=}} along with Shofuku-ji Temple, which later became the shrine’s {{ill|Bettōji|ja|別当寺|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Bettōji|qq=|comment=enwiki is a redirect}} before its abolition in the early {{ill|Meiji era|en|Meiji era|WD=Q3125096|lt=Meiji period|1=Meiji era}}.<ref>According to the ''Awa-shi'' (阿波志), compiled in 1815.</ref>
During the {{ill|Keichō|en|Keichō|WD=Q1328185|lt=Keicho era|1=Keichō}} (late 16th to early 17th century), the shrine was referred to as "Kasuga Daimyōjin" and received significant patronage from the Hachisuka clan, including an annual offering of 10 koku of rice. In 1873, it was officially renamed Kasuga Shrine and designated as a {{ill|Ken-sha|ja|県社|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ken-sha|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 近代社格制度}}. The shrine also features "Kasuga Spring" (春日水), one of the notable {{ill|Mount Bizan springs|ja|眉山湧水群|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Mount Bizan springs|qq=}}.

== History == The shrine traces its origins to a Kasuga Shrine originally enshrined in {{ill|Tomida Manor|ja|富田庄|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Tomida Manor|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 富田荘}} of [[Yamato Province]] (present-day {{ill|Iritamura|ja|入田村|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Iritamura|qq=}} in [[Tokushima City|Tokushima City]]). During the invasion of [[Awa Province]] by [[Hachisuka Iemasa]], the shrine was relocated to its current location at Ōtakiyama 1 in {{ill|Bizan Town|ja|眉山町|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Bizan Town|qq=}}. This history is documented in the *Awa-shi* from 1815 (Bunka 12). Another theory suggests that in 1586 (Tenshō 14), during the construction of [https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tokushima_Castle Tokushima Castle], the shrine was moved from {{ill|Tamiyamura|ja|田宮村|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Tamiyamura|qq=}} to serve as the castle's tutelary shrine.
Under the governance of the [[Hachisuka clan]], the shrine, known as "Kasuga Daimyōjin," gained significant reverence, receiving annual offerings of 10 koku of rice. In 1873 (Meiji 6), the shrine's name was officially changed to Kasuga Shrine, and it was designated a Prefectural Shrine. The site includes the spring known as *Kasuga Water*, part of the {{ill|Bizan Springs|ja|眉山湧水群|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Bizan Springs|qq=}}.

[[File:Kasugasui.jpeg|thumb|250px|right|Kasuga Spring (春日水)]] '''Kasuga Shrine''' (春日神社) is a {{ill|Shinto shrine|en|Shinto shrine|WD=Q845945|lt=Shinto shrine|1=Shinto shrine}} located in {{ill|Myozan, Tokushima City|ja|眉山町|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Myozan, Tokushima City|qq=}}, {{ill|Tokushima Prefecture|en|Tokushima Prefecture|WD=Q160734|lt=Tokushima Prefecture|1=Tokushima Prefecture}}, Japan. It is situated on the eastern foothills of {{ill|Mount Bizan|ja|眉山|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Mount Bizan|qq=}}.
== Deities == The shrine enshrines the following four {{ill|Column|en|Column|WD=Q4817|lt=Kami|1=Column}} (deities), identical to those of {{ill|Kasuga-taisha|en|Kasuga-taisha|WD=Q714559|lt=Kasuga-taisha|1=Kasuga-taisha}} in {{ill|Nara Prefecture|en|Nara Prefecture|WD=Q131287|lt=Nara Prefecture|1=Nara Prefecture}}: * {{ill|Takemikazuchi|ja|武甕槌命|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Takemikazuchi|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to タケミカヅチ}} * {{ill|Izanagi-no-Mikoto|ja|斎主命|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Izanagi-no-Mikoto|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 経津主神}} * {{ill|Amenokoyane no Mikoto|ja|天児屋根命|1=Ame-no-Koyane|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Amenokoyane no Mikoto|13=User:Immanuelle/Ame-no-Koyane|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 天児屋命}} * {{ill|Himegami|en|Himegami|WD=Q22070227|lt=Hime no Kami|1=Himegami}}
== History == The shrine traces its origins to a {{ill|Kasuga-taisha|lt=Kasuga-taisha|lt=Kasuga Shrine|ja|春日祠|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kasuga Shrine|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}} enshrined at the Kasuga territory in {{ill|Tomi-da|ja|富田庄|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Tomi-da|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 富田荘}} (modern {{ill|Irida|ja|入田町|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Irida|qq=}}, Tokushima City), a former estate of Kasuga Shrine in {{ill|Yamato Province|en|Yamato Province|WD=Q907495|lt=Yamato Province|1=Yamato Province}}. It is said to have been relocated to its current site at Otakiyama during the transfer of power to the {{ill|Hachisuka clan|en|Hachisuka clan|WD=Q2975261|lt=Hachisuka clan|1=Hachisuka clan}} in 1586, coinciding with the construction of {{ill|Tokushima Castle|en|Tokushima Castle|WD=Q8011246|lt=Tokushima Castle|1=Tokushima Castle}}. Another account suggests the shrine was moved from {{ill|Tamiya Village|ja|田宮村|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Tamiya Village|qq=}} along with Shofuku-ji Temple, which later became the shrine’s {{ill|Bettōji|ja|別当寺|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Bettōji|qq=|comment=enwiki is a redirect}} before its abolition in the early {{ill|Meiji era|en|Meiji era|WD=Q3125096|lt=Meiji period|1=Meiji era}}.<ref>According to the ''Awa-shi'' (阿波志), compiled in 1815.</ref>
During the {{ill|Keichō|en|Keichō|WD=Q1328185|lt=Keicho era|1=Keichō}} (late 16th to early 17th century), the shrine was referred to as "Kasuga Daimyōjin" and received significant patronage from the Hachisuka clan, including an annual offering of 10 koku of rice. In 1873, it was officially renamed Kasuga Shrine and designated as a {{ill|Ken-sha|ja|県社|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ken-sha|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 近代社格制度}}. The shrine also features "Kasuga Spring" (春日水), one of the notable {{ill|Mount Bizan springs|ja|眉山湧水群|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Mount Bizan springs|qq=}}.
== Sub-Shrines == The shrine complex includes the following sub-shrines: * '''Toyotama-hime Shrine''' (deity: {{ill|Toyotama-hime|ja|豊玉比賣|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Toyotama-hime|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}}) ** Enshrines the deity formerly worshipped at Ryuo Shrine within Tokushima Castle. * '''Wakamiya Shrine''' (deity: {{ill|Ame-no-Kumunushi|ja|天忍雲根命|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ame-no-Kumunushi|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 天押雲根命}}) * '''Akiba Shrine''' (deity: {{ill|Amaterasu|ja|天照大御神|1=Amaterasu|lt=Amaterasu Ōmikami|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Amaterasu|13=User:Immanuelle/Amaterasu|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 天照大神}}, {{ill|Onamuchi|ja|大巳貴命|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Onamuchi|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 大国主}}, {{ill|Haniyasubime|ja|埴安姫神|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Haniyasubime|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}}, {{ill|Ukemochi|en|Ukemochi|WD=Q2280323|lt=Ukemochi|1=Ukemochi}}, {{ill|Sukunabikona|ja|少彦名命|1=Sukunabikona|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Sukunabikona|13=User:Immanuelle/Sukunabikona|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to スクナビコナ}})
== Transportation == * '''By car''': 5 minutes from {{ill|Tokushima Station|en|Tokushima Station|WD=Q860775|lt=Tokushima Station|1=Tokushima Station}}, {{ill|Shikoku Railway Company|en|Shikoku Railway Company|WD=Q496531|lt=Shikoku Railway Company|1=Shikoku Railway Company}} (JR Shikoku).

It is situated at the eastern foot of Mount Ōtakiyama within Bizan.

== History == The shrine traces its origins to a Kasuga Shrine originally enshrined in {{ill|Tomida Manor|ja|富田庄|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Tomida Manor|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 富田荘}} of [[Yamato Province]] (present-day {{ill|Iritamura|ja|入田村|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Iritamura|qq=}} in [[Tokushima City|Tokushima City]]). During the invasion of [[Awa Province]] by [[Hachisuka Iemasa]], the shrine was relocated to its current location at Ōtakiyama 1 in {{ill|Bizan Town|ja|眉山町|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Bizan Town|qq=}}. This history is documented in the *Awa-shi* from 1815 (Bunka 12). Another theory suggests that in 1586 (Tenshō 14), during the construction of [https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tokushima_Castle Tokushima Castle], the shrine was moved from {{ill|Tamiyamura|ja|田宮村|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Tamiyamura|qq=}} to serve as the castle's tutelary shrine.
Under the governance of the [[Hachisuka clan]], the shrine, known as "Kasuga Daimyōjin," gained significant reverence, receiving annual offerings of 10 koku of rice. In 1873 (Meiji 6), the shrine's name was officially changed to Kasuga Shrine, and it was designated a Prefectural Shrine. The site includes the spring known as *Kasuga Water*, part of the {{ill|Bizan Springs|ja|眉山湧水群|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Bizan Springs|qq=}}.
== Subsidiary Shrines == * '''Toyotama-Hime Shrine''' (deity: [[Toyotama-hime|Toyotama-Hime-no-Mikoto]], designated as an ancient shrine) ''' The shrine was originally located within [https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tokushima_Castle Tokushima Castle] as Ryūō Shrine, later merged into Kunikazu Shrine before being relocated here. * '''Wakamiya Shrine''' (deity: {{ill|Ame-no-Oshikumone|ja|天押雲根命|en|draft:Ame-no-Oshikumone|simple|User:Immanuelle/Ame-no-Oshikumone|fr|Utilisateur:Immanuelle/Ame-no-Oshikumone|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ame-no-Oshikumone|qq=}}) * '''Akiba Shrine''' (deity: [[Amaterasu]], [[Ōkuninushi|Ōkuninushi-no-Mikoto]], [[Haniyasu-hiko and Haniyasu-hime|Haniyasu-hime-no-Mikoto]], [[Ukemochi|Ukemochi-no-Kami]], [[Sukunabikona|Sukunahikona-no-Kami]])
== Transportation == * Approximately 5 minutes by car from [[JR Tokushima Station]].

[[File:Kasugasui.jpeg|thumb|250px|right|Kasuga Spring (春日水)]] '''Kasuga Shrine''' (春日神社) is a {{ill|Shinto shrine|en|Shinto shrine|WD=Q845945|lt=Shinto shrine|1=Shinto shrine}} located in {{ill|Myozan, Tokushima City|ja|眉山町|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Myozan, Tokushima City|qq=}}, {{ill|Tokushima Prefecture|en|Tokushima Prefecture|WD=Q160734|lt=Tokushima Prefecture|1=Tokushima Prefecture}}, Japan. It is situated on the eastern foothills of {{ill|Mount Bizan|ja|眉山|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Mount Bizan|qq=}}.
== Deities == The shrine enshrines the following four {{ill|Column|en|Column|WD=Q4817|lt=Kami|1=Column}} (deities), identical to those of {{ill|Kasuga-taisha|en|Kasuga-taisha|WD=Q714559|lt=Kasuga-taisha|1=Kasuga-taisha}} in {{ill|Nara Prefecture|en|Nara Prefecture|WD=Q131287|lt=Nara Prefecture|1=Nara Prefecture}}: * {{ill|Takemikazuchi|ja|武甕槌命|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Takemikazuchi|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to タケミカヅチ}} * {{ill|Izanagi-no-Mikoto|ja|斎主命|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Izanagi-no-Mikoto|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 経津主神}} * {{ill|Amenokoyane no Mikoto|ja|天児屋根命|1=Ame-no-Koyane|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Amenokoyane no Mikoto|13=User:Immanuelle/Ame-no-Koyane|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 天児屋命}} * {{ill|Himegami|en|Himegami|WD=Q22070227|lt=Hime no Kami|1=Himegami}}
== History == The shrine traces its origins to a {{ill|Kasuga-taisha|lt=Kasuga-taisha|lt=Kasuga Shrine|ja|春日祠|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kasuga Shrine|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}} enshrined at the Kasuga territory in {{ill|Tomi-da|ja|富田庄|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Tomi-da|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 富田荘}} (modern {{ill|Irida|ja|入田町|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Irida|qq=}}, Tokushima City), a former estate of Kasuga Shrine in {{ill|Yamato Province|en|Yamato Province|WD=Q907495|lt=Yamato Province|1=Yamato Province}}. It is said to have been relocated to its current site at Otakiyama during the transfer of power to the {{ill|Hachisuka clan|en|Hachisuka clan|WD=Q2975261|lt=Hachisuka clan|1=Hachisuka clan}} in 1586, coinciding with the construction of {{ill|Tokushima Castle|en|Tokushima Castle|WD=Q8011246|lt=Tokushima Castle|1=Tokushima Castle}}. Another account suggests the shrine was moved from {{ill|Tamiya Village|ja|田宮村|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Tamiya Village|qq=}} along with Shofuku-ji Temple, which later became the shrine’s {{ill|Bettōji|ja|別当寺|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Bettōji|qq=|comment=enwiki is a redirect}} before its abolition in the early {{ill|Meiji era|en|Meiji era|WD=Q3125096|lt=Meiji period|1=Meiji era}}.<ref>According to the ''Awa-shi'' (阿波志), compiled in 1815.</ref>
During the {{ill|Keichō|en|Keichō|WD=Q1328185|lt=Keicho era|1=Keichō}} (late 16th to early 17th century), the shrine was referred to as "Kasuga Daimyōjin" and received significant patronage from the Hachisuka clan, including an annual offering of 10 koku of rice. In 1873, it was officially renamed Kasuga Shrine and designated as a {{ill|Ken-sha|ja|県社|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ken-sha|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 近代社格制度}}. The shrine also features "Kasuga Spring" (春日水), one of the notable {{ill|Mount Bizan springs|ja|眉山湧水群|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Mount Bizan springs|qq=}}.

== History == The shrine traces its origins to a Kasuga Shrine originally enshrined in {{ill|Tomida Manor|ja|富田庄|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Tomida Manor|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 富田荘}} of [[Yamato Province]] (present-day {{ill|Iritamura|ja|入田村|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Iritamura|qq=}} in [[Tokushima City|Tokushima City]]). During the invasion of [[Awa Province]] by [[Hachisuka Iemasa]], the shrine was relocated to its current location at Ōtakiyama 1 in {{ill|Bizan Town|ja|眉山町|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Bizan Town|qq=}}. This history is documented in the *Awa-shi* from 1815 (Bunka 12). Another theory suggests that in 1586 (Tenshō 14), during the construction of [https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tokushima_Castle Tokushima Castle], the shrine was moved from {{ill|Tamiyamura|ja|田宮村|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Tamiyamura|qq=}} to serve as the castle's tutelary shrine.
Under the governance of the [[Hachisuka clan]], the shrine, known as "Kasuga Daimyōjin," gained significant reverence, receiving annual offerings of 10 koku of rice. In 1873 (Meiji 6), the shrine's name was officially changed to Kasuga Shrine, and it was designated a Prefectural Shrine. The site includes the spring known as *Kasuga Water*, part of the {{ill|Bizan Springs|ja|眉山湧水群|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Bizan Springs|qq=}}.

[[File:Kasugasui.jpeg|thumb|250px|right|Kasuga Spring (春日水)]] '''Kasuga Shrine''' (春日神社) is a {{ill|Shinto shrine|en|Shinto shrine|WD=Q845945|lt=Shinto shrine|1=Shinto shrine}} located in {{ill|Myozan, Tokushima City|ja|眉山町|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Myozan, Tokushima City|qq=}}, {{ill|Tokushima Prefecture|en|Tokushima Prefecture|WD=Q160734|lt=Tokushima Prefecture|1=Tokushima Prefecture}}, Japan. It is situated on the eastern foothills of {{ill|Mount Bizan|ja|眉山|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Mount Bizan|qq=}}.
== Deities == The shrine enshrines the following four {{ill|Column|en|Column|WD=Q4817|lt=Kami|1=Column}} (deities), identical to those of {{ill|Kasuga-taisha|en|Kasuga-taisha|WD=Q714559|lt=Kasuga-taisha|1=Kasuga-taisha}} in {{ill|Nara Prefecture|en|Nara Prefecture|WD=Q131287|lt=Nara Prefecture|1=Nara Prefecture}}: * {{ill|Takemikazuchi|ja|武甕槌命|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Takemikazuchi|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to タケミカヅチ}} * {{ill|Izanagi-no-Mikoto|ja|斎主命|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Izanagi-no-Mikoto|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 経津主神}} * {{ill|Amenokoyane no Mikoto|ja|天児屋根命|1=Ame-no-Koyane|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Amenokoyane no Mikoto|13=User:Immanuelle/Ame-no-Koyane|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 天児屋命}} * {{ill|Himegami|en|Himegami|WD=Q22070227|lt=Hime no Kami|1=Himegami}}
== History == The shrine traces its origins to a {{ill|Kasuga-taisha|lt=Kasuga-taisha|lt=Kasuga Shrine|ja|春日祠|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kasuga Shrine|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}} enshrined at the Kasuga territory in {{ill|Tomi-da|ja|富田庄|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Tomi-da|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 富田荘}} (modern {{ill|Irida|ja|入田町|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Irida|qq=}}, Tokushima City), a former estate of Kasuga Shrine in {{ill|Yamato Province|en|Yamato Province|WD=Q907495|lt=Yamato Province|1=Yamato Province}}. It is said to have been relocated to its current site at Otakiyama during the transfer of power to the {{ill|Hachisuka clan|en|Hachisuka clan|WD=Q2975261|lt=Hachisuka clan|1=Hachisuka clan}} in 1586, coinciding with the construction of {{ill|Tokushima Castle|en|Tokushima Castle|WD=Q8011246|lt=Tokushima Castle|1=Tokushima Castle}}. Another account suggests the shrine was moved from {{ill|Tamiya Village|ja|田宮村|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Tamiya Village|qq=}} along with Shofuku-ji Temple, which later became the shrine’s {{ill|Bettōji|ja|別当寺|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Bettōji|qq=|comment=enwiki is a redirect}} before its abolition in the early {{ill|Meiji era|en|Meiji era|WD=Q3125096|lt=Meiji period|1=Meiji era}}.<ref>According to the ''Awa-shi'' (阿波志), compiled in 1815.</ref>
During the {{ill|Keichō|en|Keichō|WD=Q1328185|lt=Keicho era|1=Keichō}} (late 16th to early 17th century), the shrine was referred to as "Kasuga Daimyōjin" and received significant patronage from the Hachisuka clan, including an annual offering of 10 koku of rice. In 1873, it was officially renamed Kasuga Shrine and designated as a {{ill|Ken-sha|ja|県社|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ken-sha|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 近代社格制度}}. The shrine also features "Kasuga Spring" (春日水), one of the notable {{ill|Mount Bizan springs|ja|眉山湧水群|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Mount Bizan springs|qq=}}.
== Sub-Shrines == The shrine complex includes the following sub-shrines: * '''Toyotama-hime Shrine''' (deity: {{ill|Toyotama-hime|ja|豊玉比賣|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Toyotama-hime|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}}) ** Enshrines the deity formerly worshipped at Ryuo Shrine within Tokushima Castle. * '''Wakamiya Shrine''' (deity: {{ill|Ame-no-Kumunushi|ja|天忍雲根命|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ame-no-Kumunushi|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 天押雲根命}}) * '''Akiba Shrine''' (deity: {{ill|Amaterasu|ja|天照大御神|1=Amaterasu|lt=Amaterasu Ōmikami|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Amaterasu|13=User:Immanuelle/Amaterasu|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 天照大神}}, {{ill|Onamuchi|ja|大巳貴命|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Onamuchi|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 大国主}}, {{ill|Haniyasubime|ja|埴安姫神|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Haniyasubime|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}}, {{ill|Ukemochi|en|Ukemochi|WD=Q2280323|lt=Ukemochi|1=Ukemochi}}, {{ill|Sukunabikona|ja|少彦名命|1=Sukunabikona|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Sukunabikona|13=User:Immanuelle/Sukunabikona|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to スクナビコナ}})
== Transportation == * '''By car''': 5 minutes from {{ill|Tokushima Station|en|Tokushima Station|WD=Q860775|lt=Tokushima Station|1=Tokushima Station}}, {{ill|Shikoku Railway Company|en|Shikoku Railway Company|WD=Q496531|lt=Shikoku Railway Company|1=Shikoku Railway Company}} (JR Shikoku).

== History == The shrine traces its origins to a Kasuga Shrine originally enshrined in {{ill|Tomida Manor|ja|富田庄|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Tomida Manor|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 富田荘}} of [[Yamato Province]] (present-day {{ill|Iritamura|ja|入田村|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Iritamura|qq=}} in [[Tokushima City|Tokushima City]]). During the invasion of [[Awa Province]] by [[Hachisuka Iemasa]], the shrine was relocated to its current location at Ōtakiyama 1 in {{ill|Bizan Town|ja|眉山町|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Bizan Town|qq=}}. This history is documented in the *Awa-shi* from 1815 (Bunka 12). Another theory suggests that in 1586 (Tenshō 14), during the construction of [https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tokushima_Castle Tokushima Castle], the shrine was moved from {{ill|Tamiyamura|ja|田宮村|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Tamiyamura|qq=}} to serve as the castle's tutelary shrine.
Under the governance of the [[Hachisuka clan]], the shrine, known as "Kasuga Daimyōjin," gained significant reverence, receiving annual offerings of 10 koku of rice. In 1873 (Meiji 6), the shrine's name was officially changed to Kasuga Shrine, and it was designated a Prefectural Shrine. The site includes the spring known as *Kasuga Water*, part of the {{ill|Bizan Springs|ja|眉山湧水群|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Bizan Springs|qq=}}.
== Subsidiary Shrines == * '''Toyotama-Hime Shrine''' (deity: [[Toyotama-hime|Toyotama-Hime-no-Mikoto]], designated as an ancient shrine) ''' The shrine was originally located within [https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tokushima_Castle Tokushima Castle] as Ryūō Shrine, later merged into Kunikazu Shrine before being relocated here. * '''Wakamiya Shrine''' (deity: {{ill|Ame-no-Oshikumone|ja|天押雲根命|en|draft:Ame-no-Oshikumone|simple|User:Immanuelle/Ame-no-Oshikumone|fr|Utilisateur:Immanuelle/Ame-no-Oshikumone|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ame-no-Oshikumone|qq=}}) * '''Akiba Shrine''' (deity: [[Amaterasu]], [[Ōkuninushi|Ōkuninushi-no-Mikoto]], [[Haniyasu-hiko and Haniyasu-hime|Haniyasu-hime-no-Mikoto]], [[Ukemochi|Ukemochi-no-Kami]], [[Sukunabikona|Sukunahikona-no-Kami]])

[[File:Kasugasui.jpeg|thumb|250px|right|Kasuga Spring (春日水)]] '''Kasuga Shrine''' (春日神社) is a {{ill|Shinto shrine|en|Shinto shrine|WD=Q845945|lt=Shinto shrine|1=Shinto shrine}} located in {{ill|Myozan, Tokushima City|ja|眉山町|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Myozan, Tokushima City|qq=}}, {{ill|Tokushima Prefecture|en|Tokushima Prefecture|WD=Q160734|lt=Tokushima Prefecture|1=Tokushima Prefecture}}, Japan. It is situated on the eastern foothills of {{ill|Mount Bizan|ja|眉山|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Mount Bizan|qq=}}.
== Deities == The shrine enshrines the following four {{ill|Column|en|Column|WD=Q4817|lt=Kami|1=Column}} (deities), identical to those of {{ill|Kasuga-taisha|en|Kasuga-taisha|WD=Q714559|lt=Kasuga-taisha|1=Kasuga-taisha}} in {{ill|Nara Prefecture|en|Nara Prefecture|WD=Q131287|lt=Nara Prefecture|1=Nara Prefecture}}: * {{ill|Takemikazuchi|ja|武甕槌命|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Takemikazuchi|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to タケミカヅチ}} * {{ill|Izanagi-no-Mikoto|ja|斎主命|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Izanagi-no-Mikoto|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 経津主神}} * {{ill|Amenokoyane no Mikoto|ja|天児屋根命|1=Ame-no-Koyane|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Amenokoyane no Mikoto|13=User:Immanuelle/Ame-no-Koyane|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 天児屋命}} * {{ill|Himegami|en|Himegami|WD=Q22070227|lt=Hime no Kami|1=Himegami}}
== History == The shrine traces its origins to a {{ill|Kasuga-taisha|lt=Kasuga-taisha|lt=Kasuga Shrine|ja|春日祠|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kasuga Shrine|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}} enshrined at the Kasuga territory in {{ill|Tomi-da|ja|富田庄|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Tomi-da|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 富田荘}} (modern {{ill|Irida|ja|入田町|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Irida|qq=}}, Tokushima City), a former estate of Kasuga Shrine in {{ill|Yamato Province|en|Yamato Province|WD=Q907495|lt=Yamato Province|1=Yamato Province}}. It is said to have been relocated to its current site at Otakiyama during the transfer of power to the {{ill|Hachisuka clan|en|Hachisuka clan|WD=Q2975261|lt=Hachisuka clan|1=Hachisuka clan}} in 1586, coinciding with the construction of {{ill|Tokushima Castle|en|Tokushima Castle|WD=Q8011246|lt=Tokushima Castle|1=Tokushima Castle}}. Another account suggests the shrine was moved from {{ill|Tamiya Village|ja|田宮村|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Tamiya Village|qq=}} along with Shofuku-ji Temple, which later became the shrine’s {{ill|Bettōji|ja|別当寺|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Bettōji|qq=|comment=enwiki is a redirect}} before its abolition in the early {{ill|Meiji era|en|Meiji era|WD=Q3125096|lt=Meiji period|1=Meiji era}}.<ref>According to the ''Awa-shi'' (阿波志), compiled in 1815.</ref>
During the {{ill|Keichō|en|Keichō|WD=Q1328185|lt=Keicho era|1=Keichō}} (late 16th to early 17th century), the shrine was referred to as "Kasuga Daimyōjin" and received significant patronage from the Hachisuka clan, including an annual offering of 10 koku of rice. In 1873, it was officially renamed Kasuga Shrine and designated as a {{ill|Ken-sha|ja|県社|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ken-sha|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 近代社格制度}}. The shrine also features "Kasuga Spring" (春日水), one of the notable {{ill|Mount Bizan springs|ja|眉山湧水群|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Mount Bizan springs|qq=}}.

== History == The shrine traces its origins to a Kasuga Shrine originally enshrined in {{ill|Tomida Manor|ja|富田庄|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Tomida Manor|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 富田荘}} of [[Yamato Province]] (present-day {{ill|Iritamura|ja|入田村|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Iritamura|qq=}} in [[Tokushima City|Tokushima City]]). During the invasion of [[Awa Province]] by [[Hachisuka Iemasa]], the shrine was relocated to its current location at Ōtakiyama 1 in {{ill|Bizan Town|ja|眉山町|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Bizan Town|qq=}}. This history is documented in the *Awa-shi* from 1815 (Bunka 12). Another theory suggests that in 1586 (Tenshō 14), during the construction of [https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tokushima_Castle Tokushima Castle], the shrine was moved from {{ill|Tamiyamura|ja|田宮村|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Tamiyamura|qq=}} to serve as the castle's tutelary shrine.
Under the governance of the [[Hachisuka clan]], the shrine, known as "Kasuga Daimyōjin," gained significant reverence, receiving annual offerings of 10 koku of rice. In 1873 (Meiji 6), the shrine's name was officially changed to Kasuga Shrine, and it was designated a Prefectural Shrine. The site includes the spring known as *Kasuga Water*, part of the {{ill|Bizan Springs|ja|眉山湧水群|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Bizan Springs|qq=}}.

During the {{ill|Keichō|en|Keichō|WD=Q1328185|lt=Keicho era|1=Keichō}} (late 16th to early 17th century), the shrine was referred to as "Kasuga Daimyōjin" and received significant patronage from the Hachisuka clan, including an annual offering of 10 koku of rice. In 1873, it was officially renamed Kasuga Shrine and designated as a {{ill|Ken-sha|ja|県社|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ken-sha|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 近代社格制度}}. The shrine also features "Kasuga Spring" (春日水), one of the notable {{ill|Mount Bizan springs|ja|眉山湧水群|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Mount Bizan springs|qq=}}.

== History == The shrine traces its origins to a Kasuga Shrine originally enshrined in {{ill|Tomida Manor|ja|富田庄|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Tomida Manor|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 富田荘}} of [[Yamato Province]] (present-day {{ill|Iritamura|ja|入田村|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Iritamura|qq=}} in [[Tokushima City|Tokushima City]]). During the invasion of [[Awa Province]] by [[Hachisuka Iemasa]], the shrine was relocated to its current location at Ōtakiyama 1 in {{ill|Bizan Town|ja|眉山町|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Bizan Town|qq=}}. This history is documented in the *Awa-shi* from 1815 (Bunka 12). Another theory suggests that in 1586 (Tenshō 14), during the construction of [https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tokushima_Castle Tokushima Castle], the shrine was moved from {{ill|Tamiyamura|ja|田宮村|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Tamiyamura|qq=}} to serve as the castle's tutelary shrine.
Under the governance of the [[Hachisuka clan]], the shrine, known as "Kasuga Daimyōjin," gained significant reverence, receiving annual offerings of 10 koku of rice. In 1873 (Meiji 6), the shrine's name was officially changed to Kasuga Shrine, and it was designated a Prefectural Shrine. The site includes the spring known as *Kasuga Water*, part of the {{ill|Bizan Springs|ja|眉山湧水群|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Bizan Springs|qq=}}.

'''Kasuga Shrine''' (春日神社) is a Shinto shrine located in {{ill|Bizan Town|ja|眉山町|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Bizan Town|qq=}}, [[Tokushima (city)|Tokushima City]], [[Tokushima Prefecture|Tokushima Prefecture]], Japan. == History == The shrine traces its origins to a Kasuga Shrine originally enshrined in {{ill|Tomida Manor|ja|富田庄|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Tomida Manor|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 富田荘}} of [[Yamato Province]] (present-day {{ill|Iritamura|ja|入田村|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Iritamura|qq=}} in [[Tokushima City|Tokushima City]]). During the invasion of [[Awa Province]] by [[Hachisuka Iemasa]], the shrine was relocated to its current location at Ōtakiyama 1 in {{ill|Bizan Town|ja|眉山町|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Bizan Town|qq=}}. This history is documented in the *Awa-shi* from 1815 (Bunka 12). Another theory suggests that in 1586 (Tenshō 14), during the construction of [https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tokushima_Castle Tokushima Castle], the shrine was moved from {{ill|Tamiyamura|ja|田宮村|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Tamiyamura|qq=}} to serve as the castle's tutelary shrine.
Under the governance of the [[Hachisuka clan]], the shrine, known as "Kasuga Daimyōjin," gained significant reverence, receiving annual offerings of 10 koku of rice. In 1873 (Meiji 6), the shrine's name was officially changed to Kasuga Shrine, and it was designated a Prefectural Shrine. The site includes the spring known as *Kasuga Water*, part of the {{ill|Bizan Springs|ja|眉山湧水群|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Bizan Springs|qq=}}.

[[File:Kasugasui.jpeg|thumb|250px|right|Kasuga Spring (春日水)]] '''Kasuga Shrine''' (春日神社) is a {{ill|Shinto shrine|en|Shinto shrine|WD=Q845945|lt=Shinto shrine|1=Shinto shrine}} located in {{ill|Myozan, Tokushima City|ja|眉山町|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Myozan, Tokushima City|qq=}}, {{ill|Tokushima Prefecture|en|Tokushima Prefecture|WD=Q160734|lt=Tokushima Prefecture|1=Tokushima Prefecture}}, Japan. It is situated on the eastern foothills of {{ill|Mount Bizan|ja|眉山|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Mount Bizan|qq=}}.
== Deities == The shrine enshrines the following four {{ill|Column|en|Column|WD=Q4817|lt=Kami|1=Column}} (deities), identical to those of {{ill|Kasuga-taisha|en|Kasuga-taisha|WD=Q714559|lt=Kasuga-taisha|1=Kasuga-taisha}} in {{ill|Nara Prefecture|en|Nara Prefecture|WD=Q131287|lt=Nara Prefecture|1=Nara Prefecture}}: * {{ill|Takemikazuchi|ja|武甕槌命|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Takemikazuchi|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to タケミカヅチ}} * {{ill|Izanagi-no-Mikoto|ja|斎主命|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Izanagi-no-Mikoto|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 経津主神}} * {{ill|Amenokoyane no Mikoto|ja|天児屋根命|1=Ame-no-Koyane|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Amenokoyane no Mikoto|13=User:Immanuelle/Ame-no-Koyane|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 天児屋命}} * {{ill|Himegami|en|Himegami|WD=Q22070227|lt=Hime no Kami|1=Himegami}}
== History == The shrine traces its origins to a {{ill|Kasuga-taisha|lt=Kasuga-taisha|lt=Kasuga Shrine|ja|春日祠|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kasuga Shrine|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}} enshrined at the Kasuga territory in {{ill|Tomi-da|ja|富田庄|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Tomi-da|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 富田荘}} (modern {{ill|Irida|ja|入田町|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Irida|qq=}}, Tokushima City), a former estate of Kasuga Shrine in {{ill|Yamato Province|en|Yamato Province|WD=Q907495|lt=Yamato Province|1=Yamato Province}}. It is said to have been relocated to its current site at Otakiyama during the transfer of power to the {{ill|Hachisuka clan|en|Hachisuka clan|WD=Q2975261|lt=Hachisuka clan|1=Hachisuka clan}} in 1586, coinciding with the construction of {{ill|Tokushima Castle|en|Tokushima Castle|WD=Q8011246|lt=Tokushima Castle|1=Tokushima Castle}}. Another account suggests the shrine was moved from {{ill|Tamiya Village|ja|田宮村|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Tamiya Village|qq=}} along with Shofuku-ji Temple, which later became the shrine’s {{ill|Bettōji|ja|別当寺|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Bettōji|qq=|comment=enwiki is a redirect}} before its abolition in the early {{ill|Meiji era|en|Meiji era|WD=Q3125096|lt=Meiji period|1=Meiji era}}.<ref>According to the ''Awa-shi'' (阿波志), compiled in 1815.</ref>
During the {{ill|Keichō|en|Keichō|WD=Q1328185|lt=Keicho era|1=Keichō}} (late 16th to early 17th century), the shrine was referred to as "Kasuga Daimyōjin" and received significant patronage from the Hachisuka clan, including an annual offering of 10 koku of rice. In 1873, it was officially renamed Kasuga Shrine and designated as a {{ill|Ken-sha|ja|県社|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ken-sha|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 近代社格制度}}. The shrine also features "Kasuga Spring" (春日水), one of the notable {{ill|Mount Bizan springs|ja|眉山湧水群|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Mount Bizan springs|qq=}}.
== Sub-Shrines == The shrine complex includes the following sub-shrines: * '''Toyotama-hime Shrine''' (deity: {{ill|Toyotama-hime|ja|豊玉比賣|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Toyotama-hime|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}}) ** Enshrines the deity formerly worshipped at Ryuo Shrine within Tokushima Castle. * '''Wakamiya Shrine''' (deity: {{ill|Ame-no-Kumunushi|ja|天忍雲根命|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ame-no-Kumunushi|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 天押雲根命}}) * '''Akiba Shrine''' (deity: {{ill|Amaterasu|ja|天照大御神|1=Amaterasu|lt=Amaterasu Ōmikami|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Amaterasu|13=User:Immanuelle/Amaterasu|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 天照大神}}, {{ill|Onamuchi|ja|大巳貴命|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Onamuchi|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 大国主}}, {{ill|Haniyasubime|ja|埴安姫神|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Haniyasubime|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}}, {{ill|Ukemochi|en|Ukemochi|WD=Q2280323|lt=Ukemochi|1=Ukemochi}}, {{ill|Sukunabikona|ja|少彦名命|1=Sukunabikona|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Sukunabikona|13=User:Immanuelle/Sukunabikona|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to スクナビコナ}})
== Transportation == * '''By car''': 5 minutes from {{ill|Tokushima Station|en|Tokushima Station|WD=Q860775|lt=Tokushima Station|1=Tokushima Station}}, {{ill|Shikoku Railway Company|en|Shikoku Railway Company|WD=Q496531|lt=Shikoku Railway Company|1=Shikoku Railway Company}} (JR Shikoku).

== History == The shrine traces its origins to a Kasuga Shrine originally enshrined in {{ill|Tomida Manor|ja|富田庄|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Tomida Manor|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 富田荘}} of [[Yamato Province]] (present-day {{ill|Iritamura|ja|入田村|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Iritamura|qq=}} in [[Tokushima City|Tokushima City]]). During the invasion of [[Awa Province]] by [[Hachisuka Iemasa]], the shrine was relocated to its current location at Ōtakiyama 1 in {{ill|Bizan Town|ja|眉山町|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Bizan Town|qq=}}. This history is documented in the *Awa-shi* from 1815 (Bunka 12). Another theory suggests that in 1586 (Tenshō 14), during the construction of [https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tokushima_Castle Tokushima Castle], the shrine was moved from {{ill|Tamiyamura|ja|田宮村|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Tamiyamura|qq=}} to serve as the castle's tutelary shrine.
Under the governance of the [[Hachisuka clan]], the shrine, known as "Kasuga Daimyōjin," gained significant reverence, receiving annual offerings of 10 koku of rice. In 1873 (Meiji 6), the shrine's name was officially changed to Kasuga Shrine, and it was designated a Prefectural Shrine. The site includes the spring known as *Kasuga Water*, part of the {{ill|Bizan Springs|ja|眉山湧水群|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Bizan Springs|qq=}}.

== History == The shrine traces its origins to a {{ill|Kasuga-taisha|lt=Kasuga-taisha|lt=Kasuga Shrine|ja|春日祠|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kasuga Shrine|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}} enshrined at the Kasuga territory in {{ill|Tomi-da|ja|富田庄|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Tomi-da|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 富田荘}} (modern {{ill|Irida|ja|入田町|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Irida|qq=}}, Tokushima City), a former estate of Kasuga Shrine in {{ill|Yamato Province|en|Yamato Province|WD=Q907495|lt=Yamato Province|1=Yamato Province}}. It is said to have been relocated to its current site at Otakiyama during the transfer of power to the {{ill|Hachisuka clan|en|Hachisuka clan|WD=Q2975261|lt=Hachisuka clan|1=Hachisuka clan}} in 1586, coinciding with the construction of {{ill|Tokushima Castle|en|Tokushima Castle|WD=Q8011246|lt=Tokushima Castle|1=Tokushima Castle}}. Another account suggests the shrine was moved from {{ill|Tamiya Village|ja|田宮村|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Tamiya Village|qq=}} along with Shofuku-ji Temple, which later became the shrine’s {{ill|Bettōji|ja|別当寺|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Bettōji|qq=|comment=enwiki is a redirect}} before its abolition in the early {{ill|Meiji era|en|Meiji era|WD=Q3125096|lt=Meiji period|1=Meiji era}}.<ref>According to the ''Awa-shi'' (阿波志), compiled in 1815.</ref>
During the {{ill|Keichō|en|Keichō|WD=Q1328185|lt=Keicho era|1=Keichō}} (late 16th to early 17th century), the shrine was referred to as "Kasuga Daimyōjin" and received significant patronage from the Hachisuka clan, including an annual offering of 10 koku of rice. == History == The shrine traces its origins to a Kasuga Shrine originally enshrined in {{ill|Tomida Manor|ja|富田庄|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Tomida Manor|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 富田荘}} of [[Yamato Province]] (present-day {{ill|Iritamura|ja|入田村|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Iritamura|qq=}} in [[Tokushima City|Tokushima City]]). During the invasion of [[Awa Province]] by [[Hachisuka Iemasa]], the shrine was relocated to its current location at Ōtakiyama 1 in {{ill|Bizan Town|ja|眉山町|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Bizan Town|qq=}}. This history is documented in the *Awa-shi* from 1815 (Bunka 12). Another theory suggests that in 1586 (Tenshō 14), during the construction of [https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tokushima_Castle Tokushima Castle], the shrine was moved from {{ill|Tamiyamura|ja|田宮村|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Tamiyamura|qq=}} to serve as the castle's tutelary shrine.
Under the governance of the [[Hachisuka clan]], the shrine, known as "Kasuga Daimyōjin," gained significant reverence, receiving annual offerings of 10 koku of rice. In 1873 (Meiji 6), the shrine's name was officially changed to Kasuga Shrine, and it was designated a Prefectural Shrine. The site includes the spring known as *Kasuga Water*, part of the {{ill|Bizan Springs|ja|眉山湧水群|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Bizan Springs|qq=}}.

[[File:Kasugasui.jpeg|thumb|250px|right|Kasuga Spring (春日水)]] '''Kasuga Shrine''' (春日神社) is a {{ill|Shinto shrine|en|Shinto shrine|WD=Q845945|lt=Shinto shrine|1=Shinto shrine}} located in {{ill|Myozan, Tokushima City|ja|眉山町|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Myozan, Tokushima City|qq=}}, {{ill|Tokushima Prefecture|en|Tokushima Prefecture|WD=Q160734|lt=Tokushima Prefecture|1=Tokushima Prefecture}}, Japan. It is situated on the eastern foothills of {{ill|Mount Bizan|ja|眉山|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Mount Bizan|qq=}}.
== Deities == The shrine enshrines the following four {{ill|Column|en|Column|WD=Q4817|lt=Kami|1=Column}} (deities), identical to those of {{ill|Kasuga-taisha|en|Kasuga-taisha|WD=Q714559|lt=Kasuga-taisha|1=Kasuga-taisha}} in {{ill|Nara Prefecture|en|Nara Prefecture|WD=Q131287|lt=Nara Prefecture|1=Nara Prefecture}}: * {{ill|Takemikazuchi|ja|武甕槌命|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Takemikazuchi|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to タケミカヅチ}} * {{ill|Izanagi-no-Mikoto|ja|斎主命|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Izanagi-no-Mikoto|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 経津主神}} * {{ill|Amenokoyane no Mikoto|ja|天児屋根命|1=Ame-no-Koyane|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Amenokoyane no Mikoto|13=User:Immanuelle/Ame-no-Koyane|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 天児屋命}} * {{ill|Himegami|en|Himegami|WD=Q22070227|lt=Hime no Kami|1=Himegami}}
== History == The shrine traces its origins to a {{ill|Kasuga-taisha|lt=Kasuga-taisha|lt=Kasuga Shrine|ja|春日祠|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kasuga Shrine|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}} enshrined at the Kasuga territory in {{ill|Tomi-da|ja|富田庄|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Tomi-da|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 富田荘}} (modern {{ill|Irida|ja|入田町|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Irida|qq=}}, Tokushima City), a former estate of Kasuga Shrine in {{ill|Yamato Province|en|Yamato Province|WD=Q907495|lt=Yamato Province|1=Yamato Province}}. It is said to have been relocated to its current site at Otakiyama during the transfer of power to the {{ill|Hachisuka clan|en|Hachisuka clan|WD=Q2975261|lt=Hachisuka clan|1=Hachisuka clan}} in 1586, coinciding with the construction of {{ill|Tokushima Castle|en|Tokushima Castle|WD=Q8011246|lt=Tokushima Castle|1=Tokushima Castle}}. Another account suggests the shrine was moved from {{ill|Tamiya Village|ja|田宮村|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Tamiya Village|qq=}} along with Shofuku-ji Temple, which later became the shrine’s {{ill|Bettōji|ja|別当寺|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Bettōji|qq=|comment=enwiki is a redirect}} before its abolition in the early {{ill|Meiji era|en|Meiji era|WD=Q3125096|lt=Meiji period|1=Meiji era}}.<ref>According to the ''Awa-shi'' (阿波志), compiled in 1815.</ref>
During the {{ill|Keichō|en|Keichō|WD=Q1328185|lt=Keicho era|1=Keichō}} (late 16th to early 17th century), the shrine was referred to as "Kasuga Daimyōjin" and received significant patronage from the Hachisuka clan, including an annual offering of 10 koku of rice. In 1873, it was officially renamed Kasuga Shrine and designated as a {{ill|Ken-sha|ja|県社|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ken-sha|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 近代社格制度}}. The shrine also features "Kasuga Spring" (春日水), one of the notable {{ill|Mount Bizan springs|ja|眉山湧水群|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Mount Bizan springs|qq=}}.

Onmatsuri|url=https://brill.com/view/journals/jrj/9/1-3/article-p213_8.xml|journal=Journal of Religion in Japan|volume=9|issue=1-3|pages=213–247|doi=10.1163/22118349-00901002|issn=2211-8349}}</ref> |}
== History == The shrine traces its origins to a Kasuga Shrine originally enshrined in {{ill|Tomida Manor|ja|富田庄|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Tomida Manor|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 富田荘}} of [[Yamato Province]] (present-day {{ill|Iritamura|ja|入田村|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Iritamura|qq=}} in [[Tokushima City|Tokushima City]]). During the invasion of [[Awa Province]] by [[Hachisuka Iemasa]], the shrine was relocated to its current location at Ōtakiyama 1 in {{ill|Bizan Town|ja|眉山町|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Bizan Town|qq=}}. This history is documented in the *Awa-shi* from 1815 (Bunka 12). Another theory suggests that in 1586 (Tenshō 14), during the construction of [https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tokushima_Castle Tokushima Castle], the shrine was moved from {{ill|Tamiyamura|ja|田宮村|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Tamiyamura|qq=}} to serve as the castle's tutelary shrine.
Under the governance of the [[Hachisuka clan]], the shrine, known as "Kasuga Daimyōjin," gained significant reverence, receiving annual offerings of 10 koku of rice. In 1873 (Meiji 6), the shrine's name was officially changed to Kasuga Shrine, and it was designated a Prefectural Shrine. The site includes the spring known as *Kasuga Water*, part of the {{ill|Bizan Springs|ja|眉山湧水群|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Bizan Springs|qq=}}.
== Subsidiary Shrines == * '''Toyotama-Hime Shrine''' (deity: [[Toyotama-hime|Toyotama-Hime-no-Mikoto]], designated as an ancient shrine) ''' The shrine was originally located within [https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tokushima_Castle Tokushima Castle] as Ryūō Shrine, later merged into Kunikazu Shrine before being relocated here. * '''Wakamiya Shrine''' (deity: {{ill|Ame-no-Oshikumone|ja|天押雲根命|en|draft:Ame-no-Oshikumone|simple|User:Immanuelle/Ame-no-Oshikumone|fr|Utilisateur:Immanuelle/Ame-no-Oshikumone|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ame-no-Oshikumone|qq=}}) * '''Akiba Shrine''' (deity: [[Amaterasu]], [[Ōkuninushi|Ōkuninushi-no-Mikoto]], [[Haniyasu-hiko and Haniyasu-hime|Haniyasu-hime-no-Mikoto]], [[Ukemochi|Ukemochi-no-Kami]], [[Sukunabikona|Sukunahikona-no-Kami]])
== Transportation == * Approximately 5 minutes by car from [[JR Tokushima Station]].
== Related Articles == * Tokushima City Central Five Shrines: ''' {{ill|Suwa Shrine (Tokushima City)|ja|諏訪神社 (徳島市)|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Suwa Shrine (Tokushima City)|qq=}} - Located in Minamisako, Tokushima City ''' {{ill|Shisho Shrine (Tokushima)|ja|四所神社 (徳島市)|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Shisho Shrine (Tokushima City)|qq=}} - Located in Fukushima, Tokushima City ''' {{ill|Hachiman Shrine (Tokushima City)|ja|八幡神社 (徳島市)|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Hachiman Shrine (Tokushima City)|qq=}} - Located in Iga Town, Tokushima City ''' {{ill|Konpira Shrine (Tokushima)|ja|金刀比羅神社 (徳島市)|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kotohira Shrine (Tokushima City)|qq=}} - Located in Semimachi, Tokushima City

[[File:Kasugasui.jpeg|thumb|250px|right|Kasuga Spring (春日水)]] '''Kasuga Shrine''' (春日神社) is a {{ill|Shinto shrine|en|Shinto shrine|WD=Q845945|lt=Shinto shrine|1=Shinto shrine}} located in {{ill|Myozan, Tokushima City|ja|眉山町|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Myozan, Tokushima City|qq=}}, {{ill|Tokushima Prefecture|en|Tokushima Prefecture|WD=Q160734|lt=Tokushima Prefecture|1=Tokushima Prefecture}}, Japan. It is situated on the eastern foothills of {{ill|Mount Bizan|ja|眉山|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Mount Bizan|qq=}}.
== Deities == The shrine enshrines the following four {{ill|Column|en|Column|WD=Q4817|lt=Kami|1=Column}} (deities), identical to those of {{ill|Kasuga-taisha|en|Kasuga-taisha|WD=Q714559|lt=Kasuga-taisha|1=Kasuga-taisha}} in {{ill|Nara Prefecture|en|Nara Prefecture|WD=Q131287|lt=Nara Prefecture|1=Nara Prefecture}}: * {{ill|Takemikazuchi|ja|武甕槌命|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Takemikazuchi|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to タケミカヅチ}} * {{ill|Izanagi-no-Mikoto|ja|斎主命|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Izanagi-no-Mikoto|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 経津主神}} * {{ill|Amenokoyane no Mikoto|ja|天児屋根命|1=Ame-no-Koyane|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Amenokoyane no Mikoto|13=User:Immanuelle/Ame-no-Koyane|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 天児屋命}} * {{ill|Himegami|en|Himegami|WD=Q22070227|lt=Hime no Kami|1=Himegami}}
== History == The shrine traces its origins to a {{ill|Kasuga-taisha|lt=Kasuga-taisha|lt=Kasuga Shrine|ja|春日祠|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kasuga Shrine|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}} enshrined at the Kasuga territory in {{ill|Tomi-da|ja|富田庄|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Tomi-da|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 富田荘}} (modern {{ill|Irida|ja|入田町|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Irida|qq=}}, Tokushima City), a former estate of Kasuga Shrine in {{ill|Yamato Province|en|Yamato Province|WD=Q907495|lt=Yamato Province|1=Yamato Province}}. It is said to have been relocated to its current site at Otakiyama during the transfer of power to the {{ill|Hachisuka clan|en|Hachisuka clan|WD=Q2975261|lt=Hachisuka clan|1=Hachisuka clan}} in 1586, coinciding with the construction of {{ill|Tokushima Castle|en|Tokushima Castle|WD=Q8011246|lt=Tokushima Castle|1=Tokushima Castle}}. Another account suggests the shrine was moved from {{ill|Tamiya Village|ja|田宮村|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Tamiya Village|qq=}} along with Shofuku-ji Temple, which later became the shrine’s {{ill|Bettōji|ja|別当寺|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Bettōji|qq=|comment=enwiki is a redirect}} before its abolition in the early {{ill|Meiji era|en|Meiji era|WD=Q3125096|lt=Meiji period|1=Meiji era}}.<ref>According to the ''Awa-shi'' (阿波志), compiled in 1815.</ref>
During the {{ill|Keichō|en|Keichō|WD=Q1328185|lt=Keicho era|1=Keichō}} (late 16th to early 17th century), the shrine was referred to as "Kasuga Daimyōjin" and received significant patronage from the Hachisuka clan, including an annual offering of 10 koku of rice. In 1873, it was officially renamed Kasuga Shrine and designated as a {{ill|Ken-sha|ja|県社|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ken-sha|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 近代社格制度}}. The shrine also features "Kasuga Spring" (春日水), one of the notable {{ill|Mount Bizan springs|ja|眉山湧水群|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Mount Bizan springs|qq=}}.
== Sub-Shrines == The shrine complex includes the following sub-shrines: * '''Toyotama-hime Shrine''' (deity: {{ill|Toyotama-hime|ja|豊玉比賣|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Toyotama-hime|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}}) ** Enshrines the deity formerly worshipped at Ryuo Shrine within Tokushima Castle. * '''Wakamiya Shrine''' (deity: {{ill|Ame-no-Kumunushi|ja|天忍雲根命|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ame-no-Kumunushi|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 天押雲根命}}) * '''Akiba Shrine''' (deity: {{ill|Amaterasu|ja|天照大御神|1=Amaterasu|lt=Amaterasu Ōmikami|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Amaterasu|13=User:Immanuelle/Amaterasu|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 天照大神}}, {{ill|Onamuchi|ja|大巳貴命|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Onamuchi|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 大国主}}, {{ill|Haniyasubime|ja|埴安姫神|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Haniyasubime|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}}, {{ill|Ukemochi|en|Ukemochi|WD=Q2280323|lt=Ukemochi|1=Ukemochi}}, {{ill|Sukunabikona|ja|少彦名命|1=Sukunabikona|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Sukunabikona|13=User:Immanuelle/Sukunabikona|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to スクナビコナ}})
== Transportation == * '''By car''': 5 minutes from {{ill|Tokushima Station|en|Tokushima Station|WD=Q860775|lt=Tokushima Station|1=Tokushima Station}}, {{ill|Shikoku Railway Company|en|Shikoku Railway Company|WD=Q496531|lt=Shikoku Railway Company|1=Shikoku Railway Company}} (JR Shikoku).

Another theory suggests that in 1586 (Tenshō 14), during the construction of [https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tokushima_Castle Tokushima Castle], the shrine was moved from {{ill|Tamiyamura|ja|田宮村|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Tamiyamura|qq=}} to serve as the castle's tutelary shrine.
Under the governance of the [[Hachisuka clan]], the shrine, known as "Kasuga Daimyōjin," gained significant reverence, receiving annual offerings of 10 koku of rice. In 1873 (Meiji 6), the shrine's name was officially changed to Kasuga Shrine, and it was designated a Prefectural Shrine. The site includes the spring known as *Kasuga Water*, part of the {{ill|Bizan Springs|ja|眉山湧水群|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Bizan Springs|qq=}}.

== History == The shrine traces its origins to a {{ill|Kasuga-taisha|lt=Kasuga-taisha|lt=Kasuga Shrine|ja|春日祠|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kasuga Shrine|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}} enshrined at the Kasuga territory in {{ill|Tomi-da|ja|富田庄|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Tomi-da|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 富田荘}} (modern {{ill|Irida|ja|入田町|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Irida|qq=}}, Tokushima City), a former estate of Kasuga Shrine in {{ill|Yamato Province|en|Yamato Province|WD=Q907495|lt=Yamato Province|1=Yamato Province}}. It is said to have been relocated to its current site at Otakiyama during the transfer of power to the {{ill|Hachisuka clan|en|Hachisuka clan|WD=Q2975261|lt=Hachisuka clan|1=Hachisuka clan}} in 1586, coinciding with the construction of {{ill|Tokushima Castle|en|Tokushima Castle|WD=Q8011246|lt=Tokushima Castle|1=Tokushima Castle}}. Another account suggests the shrine was moved from {{ill|Tamiya Village|ja|田宮村|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Tamiya Village|qq=}} along with Shofuku-ji Temple, which later became the shrine’s {{ill|Bettōji|ja|別当寺|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Bettōji|qq=|comment=enwiki is a redirect}} before its abolition in the early {{ill|Meiji era|en|Meiji era|WD=Q3125096|lt=Meiji period|1=Meiji era}}.<ref>According to the ''Awa-shi'' (阿波志), compiled in 1815.</ref>
During the {{ill|Keichō|en|Keichō|WD=Q1328185|lt=Keicho era|1=Keichō}} (late 16th to early 17th century), the shrine was referred to as "Kasuga Daimyōjin" and received significant patronage from the Hachisuka clan, including an annual offering of 10 koku of rice. In 1873, it was officially renamed Kasuga Shrine and designated as a {{ill|Ken-sha|ja|県社|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ken-sha|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 近代社格制度}}. == Accidentally Overwritten Content == {{otheruses|Shinto shrines in Myozan, Tokushima City, Tokushima Prefecture|a shrine in Shimosuketo, Tokushima City|Kasuga Shrine (Shimosuketo, Tokushima)}} {{Infobox Shinto shrine | name = Kasuga Shrine (春日神社) | religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]] |image = [[File:Kasuga Jinjya.jpeg|250px]] | location = {{ill|Myozan, Tokushima City|ja|眉山町|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Myozan, Tokushima City|qq=}}, {{ill|Tokushima Prefecture|en|Tokushima Prefecture|WD=Q160734|lt=Tokushima Prefecture|1=Tokushima Prefecture}}, Japan | coordinates = {{Coord|34|04|19.9|N|134|32|33.4|E|scale:25000|display=inline,title}} | deity = {{ill|Takemikazuchi|ja|武甕槌命|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Takemikazuchi|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to タケミカヅチ}}, {{ill|Izanagi-no-Mikoto|ja|斎主命|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Izanagi-no-Mikoto|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 経津主神}}, {{ill|Amenokoyane no Mikoto|ja|天児屋根命|1=Ame-no-Koyane|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Amenokoyane no Mikoto|13=User:Immanuelle/Ame-no-Koyane|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 天児屋命}}, {{ill|Himegami|en|Himegami|WD=Q22070227|lt=Hime no Kami|1=Himegami}} | Rank = Former {{ill|Ken-sha|ja|県社|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ken-sha|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 近代社格制度}} | founded = 1586 (Tenshō 14) | main_building = {{ill|Kasuga-zukuri|en|Kasuga-zukuri|WD=Q3193781|lt=Kasuga-zukuri|1=Kasuga-zukuri}} | festivals = {{ill|April 17|en|April 17|WD=Q2520|lt=April 17|1=April 17}}, {{ill|October 17|en|October 17|WD=Q2962|lt=October 17|1=October 17}} }}
[[File:Kasugasui.jpeg|thumb|250px|right|Kasuga Spring (春日水)]] '''Kasuga Shrine''' (春日神社) is a {{ill|Shinto shrine|en|Shinto shrine|WD=Q845945|lt=Shinto shrine|1=Shinto shrine}} located in {{ill|Myozan, Tokushima City|ja|眉山町|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Myozan, Tokushima City|qq=}}, {{ill|Tokushima Prefecture|en|Tokushima Prefecture|WD=Q160734|lt=Tokushima Prefecture|1=Tokushima Prefecture}}, Japan. It is situated on the eastern foothills of {{ill|Mount Bizan|ja|眉山|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Mount Bizan|qq=}}.
== Deities == The shrine enshrines the following four {{ill|Column|en|Column|WD=Q4817|lt=Kami|1=Column}} (deities), identical to those of {{ill|Kasuga-taisha|en|Kasuga-taisha|WD=Q714559|lt=Kasuga-taisha|1=Kasuga-taisha}} in {{ill|Nara Prefecture|en|Nara Prefecture|WD=Q131287|lt=Nara Prefecture|1=Nara Prefecture}}: * {{ill|Takemikazuchi|ja|武甕槌命|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Takemikazuchi|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to タケミカヅチ}} * {{ill|Izanagi-no-Mikoto|ja|斎主命|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Izanagi-no-Mikoto|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 経津主神}} * {{ill|Amenokoyane no Mikoto|ja|天児屋根命|1=Ame-no-Koyane|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Amenokoyane no Mikoto|13=User:Immanuelle/Ame-no-Koyane|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 天児屋命}} * {{ill|Himegami|en|Himegami|WD=Q22070227|lt=Hime no Kami|1=Himegami}}
== History == The shrine traces its origins to a {{ill|Kasuga-taisha|lt=Kasuga-taisha|lt=Kasuga Shrine|ja|春日祠|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kasuga Shrine|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}} enshrined at the Kasuga territory in {{ill|Tomi-da|ja|富田庄|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Tomi-da|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 富田荘}} (modern {{ill|Irida|ja|入田町|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Irida|qq=}}, Tokushima City), a former estate of Kasuga Shrine in {{ill|Yamato Province|en|Yamato Province|WD=Q907495|lt=Yamato Province|1=Yamato Province}}. It is said to have been relocated to its current site at Otakiyama during the transfer of power to the {{ill|Hachisuka clan|en|Hachisuka clan|WD=Q2975261|lt=Hachisuka clan|1=Hachisuka clan}} in 1586, coinciding with the construction of {{ill|Tokushima Castle|en|Tokushima Castle|WD=Q8011246|lt=Tokushima Castle|1=Tokushima Castle}}. Another account suggests the shrine was moved from {{ill|Tamiya Village|ja|田宮村|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Tamiya Village|qq=}} along with Shofuku-ji Temple, which later became the shrine’s {{ill|Bettōji|ja|別当寺|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Bettōji|qq=|comment=enwiki is a redirect}} before its abolition in the early {{ill|Meiji era|en|Meiji era|WD=Q3125096|lt=Meiji period|1=Meiji era}}.<ref>According to the ''Awa-shi'' (阿波志), compiled in 1815.</ref>
During the {{ill|Keichō|en|Keichō|WD=Q1328185|lt=Keicho era|1=Keichō}} (late 16th to early 17th century), the shrine was referred to as "Kasuga Daimyōjin" and received significant patronage from the Hachisuka clan, including an annual offering of 10 koku of rice. In 1873, it was officially renamed Kasuga Shrine and designated as a {{ill|Ken-sha|ja|県社|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ken-sha|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 近代社格制度}}. The shrine also features "Kasuga Spring" (春日水), one of the notable {{ill|Mount Bizan springs|ja|眉山湧水群|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Mount Bizan springs|qq=}}.
== Sub-Shrines == The shrine complex includes the following sub-shrines: * '''Toyotama-hime Shrine''' (deity: {{ill|Toyotama-hime|ja|豊玉比賣|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Toyotama-hime|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}}) ** Enshrines the deity formerly worshipped at Ryuo Shrine within Tokushima Castle. * '''Wakamiya Shrine''' (deity: {{ill|Ame-no-Kumunushi|ja|天忍雲根命|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ame-no-Kumunushi|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 天押雲根命}}) * '''Akiba Shrine''' (deity: {{ill|Amaterasu|ja|天照大御神|1=Amaterasu|lt=Amaterasu Ōmikami|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Amaterasu|13=User:Immanuelle/Amaterasu|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 天照大神}}, {{ill|Onamuchi|ja|大巳貴命|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Onamuchi|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 大国主}}, {{ill|Haniyasubime|ja|埴安姫神|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Haniyasubime|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}}, {{ill|Ukemochi|en|Ukemochi|WD=Q2280323|lt=Ukemochi|1=Ukemochi}}, {{ill|Sukunabikona|ja|少彦名命|1=Sukunabikona|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Sukunabikona|13=User:Immanuelle/Sukunabikona|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to スクナビコナ}})

== History == The shrine traces its origins to a Kasuga Shrine originally enshrined in {{ill|Tomida Manor|ja|富田庄|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Tomida Manor|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 富田荘}} of [[Yamato Province]] (present-day {{ill|Iritamura|ja|入田村|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Iritamura|qq=}} in [[Tokushima City|Tokushima City]]). During the invasion of [[Awa Province]] by [[Hachisuka Iemasa]], the shrine was relocated to its current location at Ōtakiyama 1 in {{ill|Bizan Town|ja|眉山町|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Bizan Town|qq=}}. This history is documented in the *Awa-shi* from 1815 (Bunka 12). Another theory suggests that in 1586 (Tenshō 14), during the construction of [https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tokushima_Castle Tokushima Castle], the shrine was moved from {{ill|Tamiyamura|ja|田宮村|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Tamiyamura|qq=}} to serve as the castle's tutelary shrine.
Under the governance of the [[Hachisuka clan]], the shrine, known as "Kasuga Daimyōjin," gained significant reverence, receiving annual offerings of 10 koku of rice. In 1873 (Meiji 6), the shrine's name was officially changed to Kasuga Shrine, and it was designated a Prefectural Shrine. The site includes the spring known as *Kasuga Water*, part of the {{ill|Bizan Springs|ja|眉山湧水群|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Bizan Springs|qq=}}.
